Industry observers note that to identify endogenous allelic controls across the four cell lines, CTCF ChIP–seq peaks were intersected with corresponding whole-genome sequencing VCF files. SNPs exhibiting complete genotypic gradients (homozygous reference, heterozygous, homozygous alternative) were scored for CTCF motif perturbation using the JASPAR matrix (MA0139.2). Allelic positive controls were defined by severe motif disruption (\(\Delta \text{Score}\ge 6.0\), max score \( > 8.0\)), whereas negative controls exhibited preserved motif integrity (\(\Delta \text{Score}\le 0.2\), both scores \( > 8.0\)).

To prevent cross-cell-line amplification bias, SYBR Green qPCR primers (75–150 bp amplicons) were designed using Primer3 v.2.6.1. An in silico masking pipeline strictly discarded any candidate primer pairs whose binding sites overlapped with endogenous variants in the merged four-cell-line VCF, ensuring 100% conserved annealing kinetics across all biological samples.

Hi-ChIP was adapted from previously published protocols with some modifications91,92. Briefly, at least 1 million healthy HCASMCs (Thermo Scientific, C-017-5C, lot no. 1689414) and healthy HCAECs (ATCC, PCS-100-020, lot no. 62382179) were crosslinked with 1% formaldehyde. The initial Hi-C portion followed the Arima Hi-C protocol described in the Arima High Coverage Hi-C Kit (Arima Genomics, A410110). For the immunoprecipitation step, sheared chromatin after the Hi-C portion of the protocol was immunoprecipitated with 5 μg of H3K27ac antibody (Abcam, ab4729) with 50 μl of protein G Dynabeads (Invitrogen 10004D) and allowed to incubate overnight at 4 °C. The protein G Dynabeads were washed and the immunoprecipitated DNA was de-crosslinked at 67 °C for 2 h and eluted (50 mM sodium bicarbonate, 1% SDS). Subsequently, Dynabeads MyOne Streptavidin C1 beads (Invitrogen, 65002) were used to enrich ligated junctions as per Hi-C protocol. Library preparation was performed using the NEB Ultra II library preparation kit (NEB, E7645L), according to the manufacturer’s protocol. Twelve PCR cycles were performed using indexed primers and subsequently DNA fragments between 300 bp and 500 bp were size selected using the Omega MagBind NGS clean up Magnetic beads (Omega, M1378). The libraries were sequenced by paired-end sequencing with at least 300 million read pairs at 2 × 151-bp read length on Illumina HiSeq 4000 platforms. Raw paired-end reads in Fastq format for respective samples were processed using the Hi-CuP pipeline93 (v.0.7.4). The hg38 human genome was used as reference to generate the Hi-CuP Digest file using two restriction motifs GATC and GANTC using the hicup_digester command for running the Hi-CuP pipeline. Paired contacts were extracted from aligned filtered bam files using Samtools (v.1.13) and used as input for the pre function in the Juicer package to generate hic files94. Paired interaction counts at 5 kb resolution were extracted from the matrix, and high-confidence chromatin loops were identified using the FitHiChIP tool (v.11.0) as described previously using default parameters95. Using HCASMC and HCAEC ChIP–seq peak files as input, and initial paired interaction files, high-confidence peak-to-all interactions with a 5-kb bin size were processed using the bash FitHiChIP_HiCPro.sh script (https://ay-lab.github.io/FitHiChIP/). High-confidence chromatin interactions were sorted and indexed in bed format and converted to long-range format for visualization on the WashU browser. The overlay of Hi-ChIP, ChIP–seq and GWAS data was plotted using the locuszoomr package (v.0.3.5) and R (v.4.3.1).

Industry observers note that chIP–seq was performed as described previously with minor optimizations96. Briefly, 1 million HCASMCs and HCAECs from the same lot used for Hi-ChIP experiments were crosslinked with 1% formaldehyde for 10 min at room temperature and quenched with glycine (125 mM) for 5 min. The cells were rinsed twice with cold 1× PBS and sonicated in nuclei lysis buffer (50 mM HEPES–KOH, pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 1% Triton X, 0.1% sodium deoxycholate, 1% SDS, Takara, 1× protease inhibitor) using the Bioruptor sonicator to obtain chromatin fragments between 200 bp and 500 bp. The fragmented chromatin was immunoprecipitated overnight at 4 °C, with 5 μg of H3K27ac antibody (Abcam, ab4729) and 50 μl of protein G beads (Invitrogen, 10004D). Subsequently, the beads were washed and immunoprecipitated DNA was de-crosslinked and eluted in elution buffer (50 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5, and 10 mM EDTA). Eluted ChIP fragments were isolated using phenol–chloroform extraction method, and DNA was purified by ethanol precipitation. Library preparation was performed on the eluted ChIP DNA using the NEB Ultra II library preparation kit, according to the manufacturer’s protocol. Ten PCR cycles were performed using indexed primers and the library of DNA fragments with sizes between 300 bp and 500 bp was selected using the Omega MagBind NGS clean up Magnetic beads (Omega, M1378). The libraries were sent for paired-end sequencing, with at least 50 million read pairs at 2 × 151-bp read length on the Illumina HiSeq 4000 platform. Paired-end sequencing reads were aligned to human genome (hg38) using BWA mem v.0.7.5 (ref. 97), and reads were deduplicated using Picard v.3.4.0 MarkDuplicates. Aligned mapped reads in BAM file were used as input for peak-calling using Dfilter98 to identify significant H3K27ac peaks using the following setting: -ks = 60, -bs = 100, -Ipvalue = 8. Bigwig tracks were normalized for sequencing depths and the sum of normalized binned tag-count represents the peak height.

Industry observers note that healthy HCASMCs (Thermo Scientific, C-017-5C, lot no. 1689414) were cultured in human vascular smooth muscle basal medium (Gibco, M231500), in Smooth Muscle Growth Supplement (Gibco, S00725) and 1% penicillin–streptomycin. Healthy HCAECs (ATCC, PCS-100-020, lot no. 62382179) were cultured in Endothelial Cell Growth medium MV2 (PromoCell, C-22022).

The Lentiguide-Puro plasmid was obtained as a gift from F. Zhang (Addgene, 52963, LentiGuide-Puro) in which the non-targeting control sgRNAs and sgRNAs targeting the TSS and regulatory enhancer were annealed and ligated into the Esp3I cut-site of the Lentiguide-Puro vector using T4 Ligase (NEB, M0202) as per the manufacturer’s instructions. Ligation products were transformed into One Shot Stbl3 Chemically competent Escherichia coli (Invitrogen, C737303) and plasmids of positive clones were isolated using FavorPrep Plasmid DNA Extract Kit (Favorgen, FAPDE001-1). The CRISPR interference expression vector for Lenti-dCas9-KRAB-blast (Addgene, 89567) was a gift from G. Hon. For lentivirus production, HEK293T cells were cultured in DMEM + 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) until 70% confluency before transfection. Then, 10 μg of individual plasmids, 7.5 μg of pMDLg/RRE, 2.5 μg of pRSV-Rev and 2.5 μg of pMD2.G lentivirus packaging plasmids were co-transfected with 50 μl of polyethylenimine diluted in 3 ml of Opti-MEM I Reduced Serum Medium (ThermoFisher Scientific, 31985070). Medium was refreshed overnight with reduced 5% FBS in DMEM medium, and the expended medium was collected twice after 24 h and 48 h, respectively. Pooled supernatant was filtered through a polyethersulfone 0.45 μm filter and viral particles were concentrated using Viro-PEG Lentivirus Concentrator (Ozbiosciences, LVG100) as per the manufacturer’s instructions.

Non-targeting control_sgRNA_F: 5′-CACCGAACGTGCTGACGATGCGGGC-3′.

Non-targeting control_sgRNA_R: 5′-AAACGCCCGCATCGTCAGCACGTTC-3′.

AMOTL2_TSS_sgRNA_F: 5′-CACCGGCGCGAACAGCCAGAGCGT-3′.

AMOTL2_TSS_sgRNA_R: 5′- AAACACGCTCTGGCTGTTCGCGCC-3′.

AMOTL2_Enhancer_sgRNA1_F: 5′- CACCGTATTCATAGACATCACTAA-3′.

AMOTL2_Enhancer_sgRNA1_R: 5′- AAACTTAGTGATGTCTATGAATAC-3′.

AMOTL2_Enhancer_sgRNA2_F: 5′- CACCGATCCCTATGGAATCCTTGG-3′.

AMOTL2_Enhancer_sgRNA2_R: 5′- AAACCCAAGGATTCCATAGGGATC-3′.

At least two independent sgRNAs targeting a single regulatory element were tested against the non-targeting control. sgRNA targeting the TSS was used as positive control. Healthy HCASMCs (Thermo Scientific, C-017-5C, lot no. 1689414) and HCAECs (ATCC, PCS-100-020, lot no. 62382179) were both co-transduced in 5 μg ml−1 polybrene with lentiviral particles packaged from Lenti-dCas9-KRAB-blast (Addgene, 89567)99, and individual sgRNAs were cloned into Lentiguide-Puro backbone (Addgene, 52963)100 at a multiplicity of infection of 3. Respective HCASMC and HCAEC growth media were refreshed after 24 h of infection, and co-selection with 10 μg ml−1 blasticidin (Gibco, A1113903) and 1 μg ml−1 puromycin (Gibco, A1113803) was performed 72 h following infection. Selected cells were allowed to recover and expanded for 2 weeks before RNA isolation using Trizol Reagent (Gibco, 15596026) and Direct-Zol RNA miniprep (Zymo Research, R2052) as per the manufacturer’s instructions. cDNA conversion was performed with at least 200 ng RNA using HiScript III RT SuperMix (Vazyme Biotech, R323-01), and reverse transcription-PCR was performed using gene-specific primers to assess for gene expression.

The following reverse transcription-PCR primers were used:.

AMOTL2_F: 5′-AGTGAGCGACAAACAGCAGACG-3′.

AMOTL2_R: 5′-ATCTCTGCTCCCGTGTTTGGCA-3′.

GAPDH_F: 5′-GTGGACCTGACCTGCCGTCT-3′.

GAPDH_R: 5′-GGAGGAGTGGGTGTCGCTGT-3′.

PPIA_F: 5′-CACCGTGTTCTTCGACATTG-3′.

PPIA_R: 5′-TTCTGCTGTCTTTGGGACCT-3′.

Industry observers note that cell kinetic proliferation live-cell imaging was performed using the HoloMonitor M4 system (Phase Holographic Imaging, PHI AB) using the Cell Kinetic Proliferation assay protocol as per the manufacturer’s instructions. Non-targeting controls and AMOTL2 dCas9-KRAB CRISPRi knockdown HCASMCs were seeded and cultured in vascular smooth muscle cell medium, in smooth muscle growth supplement, at a confluence of 15,000 cells cm−2 in a 24-well vessel (VWR, 734-2325) (n = 8). The 24-well HoloLid (PHI AB, 71130) was used to enhance the visualization and tracking of cells. At least five capture areas were taken per well, and time-lapse imaging at every 30-min time interval was taken across wells over 72 h. Cellular segmentation was performed using the HoloMonitor App Suite (v.3.5.2.446). Cellular confluence was captured and normalized to baseline at 0 h.

Recent findings suggest that total RNA was extracted using Trizol Reagent (ThermoFisher, 15596026) and Direct-Zol RNA miniprep Kit (Zymo Research, R2050). At least three independent replicates were used for RNA library preparations. RNA quality and yield was assessed using Agilent RNA 6000 pico kit (Agilent, 5067-1513) for quality. Bulk RNA-seq library preparations were prepared using VAHTS Universal V10 RNA-seq Library Prep Kit for Illumina (Vazyme, NR606-01) with Ribodepletion, according to the manufacturer’s instructions. cDNA libraries were prepared using Illumina RNA Truseq indexes and quantified using Agilent Tapestation. Sequencing was performed on the NovaSeq X Plus (PE150) by NovogeneAIT Singapore, yielding 50 million raw pair-end reads. Raw Fastq files were trimmed using the trim-galore tool (v.0.65) from Babraham Bioinformatics to sequence length of 50. Paired-end reads were mapped and aligned to the human reference genome GRCh38–hg38 using STAR aligner (v.2.7.0) as per default settings and using gene annotations from GENCODE v.38. Aligned gene counts were mapped using HTSeq-count v.2.1.2 and normalized to TPM by sequencing depth and by gene length. Differential gene-expression analysis was performed using EdgeR (v.3.42.4). Contrasts were compared between non-targeting control and AMOTL2 TSS knockdown cells. A negative binomial generalized log-linear model was used to model gene counts using the glmFit function. |log[fold change]| >0.5 and FDR < 0.05 cut-offs were used to identify significantly differentially expressed genes following multiple testing correction. Figures were generated with R v.3.5.1.

Sources indicate that HCASMCs were fixed in 4% paraformaldehyde (ThermoFisher, 5090495) for 15 min at room temperature, then washed with 3× PBS for 5 min at room temperature. Cells were permeabilized with PBS with 0.1% Triton X-100 for 15 min, followed by blocking in 5% normal goat serum in PBS (blocking buffer) for 1 h at room temperature. Primary anti-Calponin (1:100) (ProteinTech, 13938-1-AP), and primary anti-α-smooth muscle actin antibody (1:100) (Sigma-Aldrich, A5228) were diluted in blocking buffer and added to permeabilized cells overnight at 4 °C. After washing with PBS three times for 5 min, cells were incubated with Alexa fluor-conjugated secondary antibodies (1:1,000) (Goat anti-mouse 594, ThermoFisher, A-11032; goat anti-rabbit 488, ThermoFisher, A-11008) and 1 μg ml−1 DAPI for 1 h at room temperature. Stained cells were washed three times for 5 min each with PBS, and images were acquired under the same laser exposure and magnification using a fluorescence microscope (EVOS M7000).

Bulk RNA-seq AMOTL2: GSE329169. Public and/or reference resources used in this study include GTEx v.8, the 1000 Genomes Project Phase 3 reference panel and the GRCh38–hg38 human reference genome. Previously published datasets used for validation or reference mapping include GSE131780, GSE175621 and GSE188422.

N.O.S. and I.M.H. conceived the study. J.M.A., T.Y. and A.B. isolated nuclei and performed 10x Multi-ome experiments on human coronary arteries. P.C.L., X.L., Y.Z., C.W.-R., C.L.M. and B.L. performed QTL analyses. M.U.S., W.-L.Q., A.T., R.A. and J.M.E. performed enhancer–gene linkage analyses. J.M.A., I.E., T.Y., M.C., R.G.G., K.J.L., Y.-H.H., R.S., C.-M.L., B.A. and N.O.S. designed and contributed to analysis of the Hi-C data. C.J.M.L., R.G., C.A.-N., W.Q.S. and R.S.-Y.F. performed in vitro Hi-ChIP, H3K27ac and CRISPR interference experiments. Q.Z., T.N., D.Y.L., M.R. and T.Q. performed in vitro CRISPR interference validation and CTCF experiments. P.C.L., H.C.P.P., Y.W., J.O., R.E.W. and A.A. performed EMSA experiments. J.M.A., T.Y., C.J.M.L., E.Y., W.-L.L., J.C., D.R.L., S.H., S.M. and S.J. designed, performed and contributed to the Perturb–seq experiments. C.J.K. analysed genotyping data. J.M.A., S.J. and N.O.S. supervised the work. J.M.A., P.C.L., T.Q. and N.O.S. drafted the manuscript with assistance from all authors. Numbers on bars indicate the total number of Mixscape-classified KD cells per condition.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal have added Club Brugge winger Carlos Forbs to their list of January transfer targets as Mikel Arteta looks to inject more pace and creativity into his attack.
  • The 22-year-old Portugal international has rebuilt his reputation in Belgium following difficult spells with Ajax and Wolverhampton Wanderers, attracting renewed interest from several Premier League clubs.
  • However, Arsenal may have to wait until next summer to secure his signature, with Club Brugge reluctant to lose one of their most influential attacking players.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal have added Club Brugge winger Carlos Forbs to their list of January transfer targets as Mikel Arteta looks to inject more pace and creativity into his attack.

The 22-year-old Portugal international has rebuilt his reputation in Belgium following difficult spells with Ajax and Wolverhampton Wanderers, attracting renewed interest from several Premier League clubs.

However, Arsenal may have to wait until next summer to secure his signature, with Club Brugge reluctant to lose one of their most influential attacking players.

According to Football Insider, Forbs features prominently on Arsenal’s shortlist of left-sided attacking targets ahead of the January transfer window.

However, Club Brugge have already informed the Gunners that the Portuguese winger is not available for a mid-season transfer, particularly with the Belgian club still competing in the Champions League.

Forbs has registered five goals and seven assists across all competitions this season, having contributed to 22 goals during the previous campaign.

The former Manchester City academy player has also impressed at international level, recently scoring Portugal’s winning goal against Wales in the Nations League.

A recent CaughtOffside report revealed that Club Brugge could demand around €30million for Forbs, who remains under contract until 2029. Manchester United and Tottenham have also been monitoring his progress.

Arsenal’s interest in Forbs is understandable, particularly given his explosive acceleration and ability to take on defenders.

Arteta’s side regularly encounter opponents who defend in compact formations, and having another winger capable of beating players individually could help create opportunities in difficult matches.

His versatility across both flanks would also provide valuable rotation and reduce Arsenal’s dependence on Bukayo Saka.

According to recent reports, however, his disappointing loan spell at Wolves cannot be completely overlooked. Performing consistently in Belgium and succeeding in the Premier League are two very different challenges.

At around €30million, Forbs could nevertheless represent an attractive alternative to some of Arsenal’s considerably more expensive attacking targets.

The Gunners should avoid paying an inflated January premium simply to overcome Club Brugge’s reluctance to sell.

Continuing to monitor his development before revisiting negotiations next summer would be a sensible approach, particularly if Forbs maintains his impressive performances in European and international football.

Arsenal consider experienced attacking addition in January to boost title ambitions.

#117388. Tech Report: What has changed in James Bond films over the decades

📅 05 Oct 2022 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1177 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: What has changed in James Bond films over the decades

📅 05 Oct 2022 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1177 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After years of speculation, Amazon MGM Studios confirmed on Monday that Robert Pattinson would be taking on the role of James Bond following Daniel Craig's departure after five hit films in the spy series.
  • This year alone, Pattinson has starred in "The Odyssey," "The Drama" and "Primetime." He is also famous for his role as "Twilight" vampire Edward Cullen.
  • The upcoming Bond movie will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, an Oscar nominee known for movies such as the "Dune" trilogy and "Arrival.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After years of speculation, Amazon MGM Studios confirmed on Monday that Robert Pattinson would be taking on the role of James Bond following Daniel Craig's departure after five hit films in the spy series.

This year alone, Pattinson has starred in "The Odyssey," "The Drama" and "Primetime." He is also famous for his role as "Twilight" vampire Edward Cullen.

The upcoming Bond movie will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, an Oscar nominee known for movies such as the "Dune" trilogy and "Arrival.".

Based on the spy novels by author Ian Fleming, the Bond franchise — about a British secret agent known for his charm and ⁠a ⁠fondness for martinis "shaken, not stirred" — is among the longest-running and highest-grossing in Hollywood history. ​​​​​​​.

The first film in the series, "Dr. No," premiered in London on October 5, 1962.

Playing the leading role, Agent 007, was an unknown actor: Sean Connery.

Recent findings suggest that in the film, we are first introduced to his character as he sits in a casino across from an attractive woman who is about to gamble away her fortune. When she asks 007 his name, the camera pans to Bond lighting a cigarette. With a smoldering look in his eye, he utters the legendary words: "Bond, James Bond.".

Shortly thereafter in the film, 007 receives an assignment to fly to Jamaica and investigate the murder of another M16 agent. He eventually tracks down a Chinese-German criminal scientist who is bent on destroying the US space program and achieving world domination.

Recent findings suggest that in principle, this story is the basis of all of 25 James Bond films. Whether the villain is Dr. No, Blofeld, Goldfinger or Le Chiffre, they all aim for one thing: world domination. But to do so, they have to get past James Bond whose gunfire and wild chase scenes inevitably spoil their looks.

Sources indicate that although many fan forums consider "Dr. No" to be one of the best Bond films, the movie would never be made in the same way today.

Firstly, one could write entire books about the omnipresent sexism and machismo that the character James Bond has displayed over the decades.

Recent findings suggest that certainly there would have to be a thick chapter dedicated to the women in his films, who are typically portrayed as naive, willingly flinging themselves into Bond's arms, seeking protection. Sometimes they are sophisticated female antagonists who lose control at the thought of hopping into bed with the secret agent.

According to recent reports, whether friend of foe, each film had at least one Bond girl — and often more: More than 60 love interests have appeared in the films. Their names, like "Honey" or "Pussy Galore" would never be acceptable today. In more recent decades, female roles in Bond films have changed — as has Bond himself.

In the last five films in which Daniel Craig has played Bond, he is seen as a man who is tough on the outside and soft on the inside — and who is not always lucky with women.

Sources indicate that aside from the portrayal of women on screen, there are also plenty of other details in "Dr. No" that haven't quite stood the test of time.

Another sign of the zeitgeist in the 1962 film is that everyone smokes, which is a no-no by today's Hollywood standards. Cigarettes are found everywhere in the old film, from the casino to the hotel bar — and even the bedroom.

According to recent reports, smoking was commonplace in the US in the 1970s, so naturally this came across on the silver screen. In the 1970s TV series "Space: 1999" people were even depicted smoking on the moon, but by the 2000s, smoking was largely banned in many parts of the world due to its health risks.

One can also note in "Dr. No" that few people are wearing seat belts. When Bond drives off in his sports car to visit a woman, he is followed and a chase scene ensues. Bond, notably, is not wearing a seat belt.

His pursuers eventually drive off a slope and die, of course — after all, they aren't wearing seat belts either and cars didn't have airbags at the time. The vehicle explodes, prompting 007 to say, "They were obviously in a hurry to get to their own funeral.".

In the older Bond films, all secretaries and receptionists are played by women, which in the 1960s, were considered standard female jobs.

Whether redheaded, blonde or brunette, secretaries are Bond's favorite targets for womanizing and they are all susceptible to his charms.

Throughout most Bond films, the agent has a romantic tension with Moneypenny, his boss's secretary, something which was not described in the original books.

It has been revealed that in the 2012 film "Skyfall" Moneypenny is given a first name: Eve, and we finally learn her backstory. In this film, she is no longer a hopeless secretary in love, but a top-trained agent who accidentally shoots Bond and is reassigned to desk duty as punishment.

In any case, today Moneypenny's job title today would probably be "Office Manager" or "Executive Assistant" rather than "Secretary.".

Recent findings suggest that in the film, Dr. No tells James Bond that he is the child of a British missionary and a Chinese woman from an upstanding family. However, the character is portrayed by Canadian actor Joseph Wiseman who is wearing makeup to make his eyes look more "Asian.".

While it used to be the norm in such movies to have East Asian characters played by white actors, today these cases of "yellowface" are frowned upon — just as it would be to wear blackface, putting black makeup on one's skin to portray a Black person.

Industry observers note that if there was a "Dr. No" remake in the future, a Chinese actor would be more likely to play this role.

Daniel Craig already paved the way in modernizing James Bond by stripping away campy gadgets, punchlines and invincibility, replacing them with a grounded, psychological and emotionally vulnerable portrayal of a post-9/11 spy.

Recent findings suggest that now it is up to Robert Pattinson to revisit the famous MI6 agent. Film critics believe his background will allow him to add dark sophistication and nonconformism to the iconic espionage role.

Throughout his career, Robert Pattinson has managed to combine roles in blockbuster hits and indie gems, from Bruce Wayne in "The Batman" to a disposable worker who is cloned every time he dies in "Mickey 17.".

Pattinson already has experience with classic spy archetypes: As the mysterious Neil in Christopher Nolan's sci-fi action thriller "Tenet," he assisted the protagonist in a time-bending espionage mission. He is also known for his eccentric personality and deadpan humor — qualities that could be useful for a modern Bond.

Industry observers note that this article was translated from German by Sarah Hucal. It was first published in 2025 and updated following news of Robert Pattinson's casting as James Bond on November 16, 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that tragic reports have emerged from the United States, confirming that a young English footballer was shot and killed in Mississippi. The local police have now shared a statement after making an arrest.

Recent findings suggest that krissh Mahatma was born in London but had moved to the US to pursue his dream of making it as a footballer. The 18-year-old striker was in his freshman year at Copiah-Lincoln Community College in Wesson, around 45 miles south of Jackson, Mississippi, where the incident took place.

Sources indicate that before moving to the US, he had played for Watford 'A' in the post-16 Community and Education Football Alliance league. Co-Lin confirmed his signing in February.

Sources indicate that as reported by the Daily Mail, Mahatma was fatally struck by a bullet after a gun was fired outside the Green Ghost Tacos restaurant in Jackson at around 3:39 a.m. on Sunday morning.

Recent findings suggest that the English footballer was with his Co-Lin Wolves teammates when they reportedly came across a drunk man outside the restaurant. After a fight broke out, a man pulled out a gun and fired into the group, hitting Mahatma.

It has been revealed that the 18-year-old was taken to a nearby hospital via a private vehicle. According to Hinds County Coroner Jeramiah Howard, this was where he died.

In a recent development, capitol Police have since arrested and charged Danny Luna, 22, with murder. The Mississippi Department of Public Safety did not elaborate on what caused the deadly confrontation. However, in a brief statement, Police Chief Mark Miller sent 'thoughts and prayers' to Mahatma's 'family and loved ones,' adding:.

"While this arrest is an important step toward justice, we recognise that nothing can ease the pain of losing a loved one.".

Mahatma had made 14 appearances in his first three months with the Co-Lin Wolves, scoring one goal in September in a 3-2 win over National Park College. Co-Lin president Dewayne Middleton issued his own statement on behalf of the college:.

"Copiah-Lincoln Community College is mourning the loss of freshman soccer player Krissh Mahatma. Krissh will be deeply missed by his teammates and the entire Co-Lin family.".

A fundraiser has been set up to support Mahatma's family and has already raised $31,851 (£24,275). It explained how the young striker was "just beginning a latest chapter of life far away from home," before adding: "His sudden passing has left his family, friends, teammates, coaches, and the entire Co-Lin soccer community heartbroken.

"Behind this tragedy is a family grieving the loss of their son and loved ones trying to make sense of a loss that feels impossible to put into words.".

It has been revealed that the owner of the Green Ghost Tacos eatery, nearby where the shooting took place, stated: "On behalf of the entire Green Ghost family, I extend my deepest and most heartfelt condolences to the family, friends, loved ones, and university community mourning the tragic loss of a young student. Our hearts are heavy, and our thoughts and prayers are with everyone affected by this devastating incident.

Recent findings suggest that "While this tragedy occurred near our establishment, we would like to clarify that Green Ghost was closed and was not conducting business at the time of the shooting. The safety and well-being of our patrons, employees, and surrounding community remain a top priority. We are committed to cooperating fully with law enforcement as they investigate the circumstances surrounding this tragic incident.

"Out of respect for the grieving family and the investigation, we will refrain from speculating or commenting further on the details at this time. Above all, we recognise that a family has suffered an unimaginable loss. We ask that the community join us in extending compassion, prayers, and support to those affected during this incredibly difficult time.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cristian Chivu wants Inter to be ‘the best version of ourselves’ in the Champions League against VfB Stuttgart this evening, with an enhancement on Lautaro Martinez.

It kicks off at San Siro at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game and PSG-Roma on the Champions League Liveblog.

The Nerazzurri’s confidence took a knock on Sunday in Serie A when they fumbled a 4-2 lead for the chaotic 4-4 draw away to Atalanta.

They are also playing catch-up in Europe, having lost the first two matches against Real Madrid and Club Brugge, then got back on track beating Shakhtar Donetsk and Feyenoord.

“We must be the best version of ourselves,” Chivu told Sky Sport Italia.

“We are well aware of the importance of this match, we are playing at home, and must give a sense of consistency to our recent good performances in the Champions League.”.

VfB Stuttgart are one point ahead of Inter in the Champions League table going into tonight’s match, as they won the first two, drew 1-1 with Atletico Madrid, and lost 2-0 away to Galatasaray.

Pio Esposito scored a hat-trick against Atalanta at the weekend and Lautaro Martinez made his comeback after more than a month out, but is not risked from the start tonight.

Recent findings suggest that “Lautaro is recovering his fitness and ready to come on in the second half. Marcus Thuram has played practically non-stop in recent months, and we need him again this evening,” explained Chivu.

First debuted in 1995, Mitreâs Ultimax ball promptly became a defining symbol in English football. A fixture on Premier League pitches throughout the 1990s, it made history as the first football to break the 100mph speed barrier.

Now, 30 years later, Mitre has reimagined the legendary ball, bringing it back with a modern twist.

The newly introduced Ultimax Pro 30th Anniversary Ball merges the classic design with cutting-edge technology, celebrating its iconic status while setting a new standard for the next generation.

It has been revealed that while the ball retains the familiar 6-panel construction, the classic white, blue, and red colourway, and the unmistakable crown logo, itâs been upgraded with advanced features. Hyperflow grooves reduce drag and a sleek pearl finish offers a nod to traditional 30th-anniversary gifts. The interior also sees improvements, with Hyperfoam cushioning now enhanced for cleaner strikes and even more power.

To mark the milestone, Mitre has launched the "The Next In Line" campaign, spotlighting the newly introduced wave of football talent carrying on their family legacies.

The campaign features rising stars such as Raphaella Wright-Phillips, granddaughter of Arsenal icon Ian Wright, Ruben Butt, son of Manchester United legend Nicky Butt, and Jacob Fowler, whose father is Liverpoolâs own Robbie Fowler.

The trio, each in vintage 95/96 kits, embody the connection between the past and the future â just as the newly introduced Ultimax Pro does itself.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City could face a major battle to retain Erling Haaland next summer, with the Norwegian striker reportedly considering a move away from the Etihad Stadium amid growing uncertainty surrounding the club.

The 26-year-old remains one of the most prolific goalscorers in world football, but City’s disappointing performances and the possibility of significant financial sanctions have fuelled speculation about his long-term future.

Barcelona are emerging as a particularly attractive destination should Haaland decide to pursue a new challenge in 2027.

According to Spanish publication El Nacional, Haaland is seriously considering his future at Manchester City, with Barcelona among his preferred destinations.

City’s recent 2-2 Champions League draw against Napoli highlighted their ongoing struggles, with the English giants managing just one victory in their last five matches across all competitions.

The uncertainty surrounding potential sanctions for City’s financial breaches has further complicated the situation.

Barcelona have long admired Haaland, and the prospect of pairing the Norwegian with Lamine Yamal would undoubtedly appeal to the Catalan giants.

An earlier CaughtOffside report also revealed that Barcelona were monitoring Haaland’s situation following developments in City’s financial case.

However, the striker remains contracted to Man City until 2034 and has not publicly submitted a transfer request.

Losing Haaland would represent an enormous setback for City, both on the pitch and commercially.

Replacing a striker of his quality would be exceptionally difficult, particularly if financial restrictions or potential sporting sanctions limit City’s recruitment capabilities.

In a recent development, from Barcelona’s perspective, signing Haaland would be a statement of intent. His exceptional finishing ability and movement could complement Yamal’s creativity and establish a formidable attacking partnership.

Industry observers note that however, Barcelona’s financial limitations remain a significant obstacle. Even if Haaland expresses a desire to leave, convincing City to accept an affordable transfer fee would be another challenge entirely.

City’s immediate priority should be restoring consistency on the pitch and demonstrating that they can continue competing for major honours.

Haaland is entering the prime years of his career, and retaining him will require more than contractual security.

City must give their most valuable player convincing reasons to believe his ambitions can still be fulfilled at the Etihad Stadium.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's often noted that whichever football team wins the battle of the midfield tends to win the game.
  • In a recent development, with that in mind, below are the 25 best midfielders in the world right now, ranked in order – and the level of talent is off the scale.
  • Arsenal, summer on summer, were looking for the final piece of the puzzle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's often noted that whichever football team wins the battle of the midfield tends to win the game. Whether it's a holding midfielder who can shut down the opposition attack, an attacking one who can chip in with goals and assists, or a box-to-box player who can do both sides well effectively, they are usually the key to how a match pans out.

In a recent development, with that in mind, below are the 25 best midfielders in the world right now, ranked in order – and the level of talent is off the scale. The following factors have been taken into consideration when forming these rankings, with players such as Jude Bellingham and Bruno Fernandes featuring.

Arsenal, summer on summer, were looking for the final piece of the puzzle. Martin Zubimendi, signed from Real Sociedad in 2025, proved to be just that, with his willingness to screen the back four, allowing those ahead of him to be free in their attacking endeavours. Not only that, but his line-breaking passes are a sight to behold, and his defensively sound nature makes him the perfect midfielder beside Declan Rice.

Still just 27 years of age, the Spaniard has plenty of years left in the tank and was vital in the middle of the park for the Gunners as he helped the club end their Premier League title drought. He faded a little towards the end of his debut season, and has found his game time dwindle of late, but that doesn't take away from his class when at his best.

Still only 19 years old, Moroccan international Ayoubb Bouaddi has found himself thrusted into Manchester City's starting lineup alongside fellow new signing Elliot Anderson in recent weeks.

A composed, ball-carrying defensive midfielder who excels at receiving under pressure, dictating tempo, and breaking lines through dribbling rather than high-volume progressive passing - he's the kind of metronome that is rare in today's game. Even while the Cityzens have struggled for form as of late, the teenager has risen above the challenges thrown his way.

In a recent development, ryan Gravenberch was one of Liverpool's best players under Arne Slot. The Dutchman was one of Jurgen Klopp's last signings but really flourished under his compatriot, who has now departed Anfield.

The confidence and calmness of his displays in the engine room, complemented by his running power that is very reminiscent of a certain Yaya Toure and neat spins reflective of old Anfield favourite Thiago Alcantara, have been a breath of fresh air for supporter. Even if Liverpool's form dropped off in 2025/26, he is easily among the finest midfielders in the world, though his defensive contributions have dried up in favour of adventure to bring about a side to his game that can be, at times, a little eccentric.

It has been revealed that scott McTominay enjoyed his career-best season in Italy under Antonio Conte just two seasons back, scoring 13 goals and providing six assists in 36 appearances across all competitions. He was instrumental in helping Napoli to their second Scudetto in three years, claiming the Serie A's Most Valuable Player award in the process.

The Scotland international could have only dreamt of times like these when he was operating as one-half of the infamous 'McFred' partnership during some of Manchester United's darkest hours in recent memory. But a disastrous World Cup campaign with the Tartan Army suggested that maybe Italy is just a safe haven for him, hence he's dropped down a few levels in this ranking since the last update.

In a recent development, one of the finest talents in the world, Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala is only going to get better in the years to come. The Germany international looks set to be the heartbeat of his side at both club and international level, but is already producing the kind of end product that many players in their prime would be proud of. Not only is he used to getting on the scoresheet, but his dribbling ability is nothing short of otherworldly.

If he continues at the pace he is currently going, then you would fancy him entering the Ballon d'Or conversation sooner rather than later. Musiala has done an admirable job from the left flank at times, but it's painfully obvious that his future lies in an attacking midfield role, and there's little doubt he will be one of the best in the world for the foreseeable future. He could be higher on this list if a recent injury hadn't hampered his progress, which lent itself to a poor World Cup cameo and a worrying start to the 2026/27 season, which has seen him fall out of favour in Bavaria.

According to recent reports, fabian Ruiz might not be as eye-catching as some of his Paris Saint-Germain teammates, hence his 24th-place finish in the 2025 Ballon d'Or race, but the role that the Spaniard plays in his side cannot be understated. The 30-year-old has been a consistent presence in Luis Enrique's team, providing balance to midfield and playing a crucial part in their domestic treble and Champions League success in 2024/25.

Ruiz played a key role as Spain won the 2026 World Cup, with head coach Luis de la Fuente often preferring the PSG star in midfield over Pedri. He's also won the Euros with La Roja, and the Nations League, and it's about time he received more recognition for his performance levels.

Nicolo Barella has been at the heart of Inter's recent successes on domestic soil and, for a brief moment in the 2024/25 campaign, looked as though he might help drag the Nerazurri to a Champions League trophy. While the Italian side were subsequently thrashed by Paris Saint-Germain in the final of the competition, that shouldn't understate just how good their number 23 can be.

Barella is a physical presence in the middle of the pitch for Inter, but is also a gifted creator. Typically used as a box-to-box midfielder for both club and country, newly introduced manager Christian Chivu asked him to operate as a playmaker in the 2025/26 campaign, with Barella pulling strings from deep. He's played the part to perfection so far, and continues to shine well into the new campaign.

The man who helped to orchestrate a World Cup win for Argentina in 2022, thus helping to secure Lionel Messi's status as the greatest footballer of all time. Alexis Mac Allister enjoyed a standout 2022/23 campaign for both club and country, and it was no surprise that Liverpool paid Brighton & Hove Albion the handsome fee of £35 million to sign him all those summers ago.

Recent findings suggest that mac Allister won the League Cup in his first season as a Liverpool player and hoisted the Premier League title under Arne Slot a campaign later. He suffered a slight drop in performance last season while playing for a Liverpool side that had been exposed by various teams, but there's no denying the Argentine remains an effective conductor compared to his peers, as demonstrated during the 2026 World Cup. This season, he has brought the kind of structure the Reds have lacked in the middle area, and it looks like he could be set to sign a newly introduced contract as a reward for his return to form.

It has been revealed that moises Caicedo was on the receiving end of plenty of criticism during his debut season in Chelsea colours. As the most expensive signing in the league's history, up until the summer of 2025, there were huge expectations placed on his young shoulders to tighten up a leaky Blues midfield instantly. He tried his best, of course, but the one-man mission often fell short.

Recent findings suggest that despite a tricky start to life at Stamford Bridge, the Ecuador destroyer picked up his performances immensely and continued to look outstanding at times last term. During a 1-0 win over Tottenham in November 2025, for example, Liverpool legend Jamie Carragher described Caicedo as "an absolute monster in midfield". Caicedo had been a regular fixture of the new regime at the club and has gone from strength to strength in west London. The only thing holding him back is his disciplinary and fitness records.

It has been revealed that much was made of the £107 million fee Chelsea coughed up for Enzo Fernandez as part of their midfield refurbishment – and it's perhaps not unfair to say the Argentine never fully repaid the Blues on the pitch. That noted, they've now managed to make a profit on the player, selling him to Man City for £125m.

The fact that he is still so young plays into his hands. The former Benfica ace, who was born and raised in San Martin, played 170 times for the West Londoners after joining for a then-record fee in January 2023, and has now taken his Premier League experience to the Etihad. Having played in two World Cup finals, winning one, he should bring a winners' mentality to Manchester as he reunites with former Blues boss Enzo Maresca, who continues to keep the faith in him as the tough times trudge along in the winter period.

NASA's Voyager 1 reaches a light-day away from Earth

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (655 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Well, imagine having to travel 3,300 years to get to your destination.
  • Recent findings suggest that imagine departing in 1977 and arriving in 2026, on November 18 at 11:16 a.m.
  • NASA's Voyager 1, a spacecraft launched almost half-a-century ago, has traveled a light-day from Earth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hate long-haul flights? Well, imagine having to travel 3,300 years to get to your destination.

Recent findings suggest that imagine departing in 1977 and arriving in 2026, on November 18 at 11:16 a.m. Central European Time to be precise, and then, not stopping but continuing the journey.

NASA's Voyager 1, a spacecraft launched almost half-a-century ago, has traveled a light-day from Earth.

A light-day is the distance light covers in 24 hours — about 26 billion kilometers (or around 16 billion miles). Put another way: Light does in one day what it took the spacecraft 49 years, two months and 11 days to do.

But Voyager 1 is not only far away, it is also traveling at an incredible speed of 61,000 km/h (38,000 mph).

In a recent development, when Voyager 1 launched, it was in sync with a planetary alignment that was as rare as the spacecraft itself — one that happens only once every 176 years. It was the alignment Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, which scientists wanted to investigate.

Once the original mission was accomplished, Voyager 1 used the planets Jupiter and Saturn to perform a gravitational slingshot.

It has been revealed that it flew close to each planet, got pulled and accelerated by their massive gravity, and swung around faster than before. And that is how Voyager 1 has achieved its speed.

In the vacuum of space, nothing slows you down.

On Valentine's Day 1990, from beyond Neptune, Voyager 1 took the only portrait of the solar system from the outside ever made by a spacecraft.

In 2012, it became the first human-made object to reach interstellar space.

It has been revealed that its journey is ongoing. In about 40,000 years — long after its plutonium power supply dies out — it will still be flying and pass by the star Gliese 445, which is more than 17 light-years away from Earth.

It has been revealed that that's light-years, not light-days. A light-year is the distance light travels in a year. It will take Voyager 1 about 18,000 years to reach the one light-year milestone.

Voyager 1 is destined to wander the Milky Way "perhaps eternally," as NASA puts it.

The spacecraft is the first human-made object ever to be one light-day away from home.

"If you want to say 'hello' to Voyager, you send your message and then you go home and you wait two days before you finally get a response," says Suzanne Dodd, the mission's project manager at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory.

According to recent reports, but you do get a response. Even today it sends back data that helps scientists on Earth.

"[It's] still working great, sending back data from a region of space no other human-made craft has ever explored," states Kareem Badaruddin, the mission manager at JPL.

No story about Voyager 1 seems complete without mentioning The Golden Record, a phonographic record, that is part of the spacecraft's cargo.

Recent findings suggest that the spacecraft is carrying other Earthly objects as messages and artefacts from Earth for extraterrestrials. But the Golden Record is what we tend to focus on because it contains soundbites representing languages and cultures from around our planet.

We're told it's very unlikely that any intelligent lifeform will ever receive the cargo or even know how to play The Golden Record.

But if they do get the record and work out how to play it, the first thing they will hear is a controversial voice — not one of Earthly unity, as was the original idea. Those are the words of Kurt Waldheim, a former UN Secretary-General (1972-81) and Austrian President (1986-92), whose concealed wartime past as a German army officer in the Balkans surfaced a decade after Voyager 1's launch. It was alleged Waldheim had participated in Nazi crimes.

By HARRY BAMFORTH, LIVE SPORTS COVERAGE REPORTER and LUKE POWER, SPORTS REPORTER.

Updated: 19:02 EST, 25 November 2026.

Relive Daily Mail Sport's coverage from Wednesday's Champions League action as Manchester United travelled to Sporting Lisbon while Liverpool took on Club Brugge.

It's not every day that you get to spend an evening with Harry Bamforth and Luke Power - and we wouldn't recommend it, either.

Thanks for putting up with us, especially when the football is hard enough to cope with as it is if you're a Manchester United fan.

Do joins us in the morning as the reaction and fall-out from the Champions League action continues interminably.

Here are the Premier League fixtures at the weekend:.

Senne Lammens' two errors cost Man United victory at Sporting.

CHRIS WHEELER AT JOSE ALVALADE STADIUM: A week into the job and Mauricio Pochettino must be getting used to the madness of Manchester United.

Liverpool revealed a bit of everything tonight: possession dominance in the first half, counter-attacking prowess in the second, and defensive solidity throughout (for the most part!).

Lewis Steele was on hand to bring you his thoughts from Belgium.

Club Brugge 0-3 Liverpool: Reds close in on qualification.

LEWIS STEELE AT JAN BREYDEL STADION: A brace for Isak and another from Wirtz fired the Reds to victory in Bruges after their strikes helped Liverpool get back to winning ways in Europe.

Lowlights if you're a Brugge fan!

Normally I post all the goals and crazy moments separately, but there were just too many tonight.

So, instead, you can catch all the chaos in the highlights on YouTube. From penalties and howlers to disallowed goals and sending-offs, this game had it all.

Rio Ngumoha is averaging 7.8 completed dribbles every match in this year's Champions League.

No player with at least 300 minutes played has done better since 2006-07. Full credit to Opta for this one. One man has done more this campaign, and that's Jeremy Doku on 11.9, but he doesn't have the 300 minutes under his belt.

Let it sink in. When we think of direct, unstoppable dribblers, we think of Lionel Messi, Neymar, Khvichia Kvaratskhelia. Oddly Thomas Partey was up there in the standings one season. But those world-class wingers, Ngumoha is up there with them for pure dribbling ability at the moment. It's a long career ahead, and you hope his spark won't be muted, but he has mad a dazzling start. If he can add goals and assists, his potential is sky-high.

Manchester United may have been done over by some decisions, I know, but not all of them were wrong.

It has been revealed that the red card for Youri Tielemans? Fair.

Recent findings suggest that the penalty conceded by Senne Lammens? Stonewall.

So that means the next stat I am about to share is a pretty damning indictment of United's season (bar the Leny Yoro red, before you all have a pop at me).

Man United have received five red cards and conceded five penalties in just 17 games across all competitions this season.

Liverpool couldn't have had a better week going into the Merseyside derby than beating Manchester United and Brugge 7-0 on aggregate.

The annoying thing for Andoni Iraola is that Victor Munoz has picked up a knock, and he had to bring on Rio Ngumoha earlier than expected as a result, so that inhibits his options and energy up front ever so slightly.

But he will be greatly encouraged by how his £100m+ men, namely Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, and Bradley Barcola, are melding. We're yet to see the best from the latter on a consistent basis. That's the final piece of the puzzle.

Wirtz is flying now - he has now scored or assisted or done both in seven of his last nine games in the Premier League and Champions League.

Everton are having a good season and will be right up for it, but Liverpool have teed themselves up for a good performance at midday on Sunday.

Weird kick-off time, by the way.

Mauricio Pochettino, Man United boss, speaking to TNT Sports:.

Industry observers note that here's the Alisson assist from earlier. Playmaker stuff from Liverpool's number one. Always thought he could have played outfield.

Manchester United just hate playing away in Europe.

United are now winless in their last seven Champions League away games (D3 L4).

Their worst-ever run is eight... which they could well match after playing their final away match in the league phase in January.

Villarreal are waiting for them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

French Football Federation (FFF) President Philippe Diallo has received UEFA backing to be a candidate in FIFA's presidential election, which will take place in March in Morocco, with criticism against current chief Gianni Infantino growing.

UEFA, European football's governing body, said it has backed Diallo "unanimously" in a bid to replace Infantino, putting it's "full support" behind the Frenchman.

Veteran Japanese official Kohzo Tashima has also revealed his candidacy, with the deadline for candidates to stand for election being November 18.

Potential candidates for the post must show letters of support from five of FIFA's 211 member associations before going through eligibility and integrity checks.

Diallo, the 63-year-old head of the FFF, is the son of a Senegalese boxing champion.

It has been revealed that he was elected as the federation's president in 2023 with a large majority. He was reelected for another four-year term in 2024.

Back in September, Diallo said the FFF had withdrawn its support for Infantino ahead of the March 2027 election, saying trust in the FIFA president had "been betrayed.".

"The way in which the governance of world football is envisaged no longer reflects us," the French football head noted of the decision.

If elected, the Frenchman would become FIFA's first black president, as well as it's third French leader after Robert Guerin and Jules Rimet, who served as the organization's first and third presidents.

Gianni Infantino has been in charge of world football's governing body since 2016.

He has been facing growing criticism since pitching a plan of sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors. The criticism of the plan was led by UEFA and its President Aleksander Ceferin.

Infantino ended up scrapping the proposal but UEFA went ahead and took FIFA to court in the US, trying to gather evidence ahead of potentially lodging a criminal complaint with Swiss authorities about alleged "mismanagement" by Infantino.

FIFA's headquarters are located in Zürich, Switzerland.

Infantino was also criticized after creating a peace prize and awarding it to US President Donald Trump last year.

The connection between Infantino and Trump came under criticism once again during the World Cup, after United States forward Folarin Balogun was allowed to take part in the round-of-16 game against Belgium despite having been shown a red card in the previous game.

The US president admitted to having personally intervened through a conversation with Infantino.

Breaking: Worse Than Lammens: Pochettino Must Drop Man Utd Star Youri Tielemans

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (603 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Givemesport

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United missed the chance to end their six-month wait for an away win as the Reds were held to a 2-2 draw against Sporting CP in the Champions League.
  • In a recent development, mauricio Pochettino looked to be on course for a first win as head coach after Bruno Fernandes scored twice to cancel out Luis Suarez's first-half opener.
  • It was the second of two huge mistakes Lammens made against Sporting.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United missed the chance to end their six-month wait for an away win as the Reds were held to a 2-2 draw against Sporting CP in the Champions League.

In a recent development, mauricio Pochettino looked to be on course for a first win as head coach after Bruno Fernandes scored twice to cancel out Luis Suarez's first-half opener. But Senne Lammens gifted Sporting a late equaliser as he failed to deal with a high ball inside the box and dropped it, allowing a thankful Suarez to tap home from close-range.

It was the second of two huge mistakes Lammens made against Sporting. Just minutes after saving a penalty from Suarez, the United goalkeeper came rushing out of his goal and clattered into Maximiliano Araujo, causing referee Szymon Marciniak to point to the spot once again. On this occasion, Suarez made no mistake by burying the ball into the bottom corner.

Although Lammens endured a horror show against Sporting, he wasn't the worst United player on the pitch.

Another 4/10 star let Pochettino down. The man in question is Youri Tielemans, who has struggled since moving to the Reds for £35million from Aston Villa in the summer and had another evening to forget, both in and out of possession at the Jose Avalade Stadium.

Lining up in a two-man defensive midfield alongside Kobbie Mainoo once again, Tielemans was unable to influence the game as much as he would have wanted. Indeed, the 29-year-old completed just 27 successful passes with an 82% passing accuracy.

Just one of his four passes into the final third were accurate, while he made just three progressive passes during his time on the pitch. While Tielemans did make one key pass, United fans are expecting much more from the midfielder, given what he did at Villa and Leicester.

Tielemans stats vs Sporting Lisbon.

According to recent reports, from a defensive point-of-view, Tielemans wasn't much better and won just 50% (6/12) of his duels. He was dribbled past once and committed a team-high four fouls. The Belgian did, however, win four tackles, made one interception, one clearance and two recoveries.

Sources indicate that tielemans' dour night ended in the 93rd minute when he was sent off for two bookable offences. He picked up his first yellow card in the first half before seeing red for a foul on Sergi Altimira.

Due to this, he will now serve a one-match ban for United's next Champions League game, which is a clash at home to Bundesliga side RB Leipzig in December.

Summing it up, Tielemans is nowhere near to the required level needed at United right now and should be dropped ahead of Sunday's huge Premier League game against Brentford.

Mainoo was much more involved against Sporting and should keep his spot in the midfield two alongside £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, who deserves a chance from the off.

Santos is much stronger off the ball than Tielemans and Mainoo, and can help bring a more defensive and solid base alongside a creative midfielder.

On this occasion, Tielemans should drop out of the side due to his form and performance against Sporting, with Mainoo keeping his place and Santos coming in.

Fernandes, who was the hero for United in Lisbon after scoring twice, would therefore retain his place in the attacking midfield role, just in front of Mainoo and Santos.

Tielemans does still have a future at United, but for the time being, Pochettino should take him out of the firing line and give him a rest, allowing Santos a chance to show what he can do.

Breaking: Welcome to the Man United madhouse, Mauricio! Man United emerge from the chaos at Sporting Lisbon with a draw as Senne Lammens joins their band of self-saboteurs in game that had it all, writes CHRIS WHEELER

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1034 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 17:18 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 19:22 EST, 25 November 2026.
  • A week into the job and Mauricio Pochettino must be getting used to the madness of Manchester United by now.
  • If it's not drones flying over the training ground, red card controversies and random divots of grass, it's his own players shooting themselves in the foot.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 17:18 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 19:22 EST, 25 November 2026.

A week into the job and Mauricio Pochettino must be getting used to the madness of Manchester United by now.

If it's not drones flying over the training ground, red card controversies and random divots of grass, it's his own players shooting themselves in the foot.

At least, Pochettino emerged from the craziness in Lisbon with a draw on a night when Bruno Fernandes celebrated his return to the Jose Alvalade Stadium with a couple of goals.

But these are the kind of nights that must drive coaches like Pochettino potty. After the carnage of Michael Carrick's final two games in charge against Roma and Aston Villa, and the rancour of the Argentine's introduction to the Old Trafford circus at Anfield on Sunday, this was another mad, mad spectacle.

Where do we start? The two acts of self-sabotage by goalkeeper Senne Lammens? United's two disallowed goals? The first was harsh on the scorer, Amad Diallo, but also Youri Tielemans who received a booking that led to his sending-off in injury-time. Or maybe that divot, which Fernandes claimed he created and then hit to put United ahead with a bizarre deflected goal?

At the end of all the chaos, United had conceded five penalties in their last five games and picked up four red cards.

Senne Lammens (left) two errors cost Man United a deserving win at Sporting as they drew.

New United head coach Mauricio Pochettino comforts Lammens at full-time after his mistakes.

According to recent reports, that is not something that will sit well with Pochettino. But after venting his frustration with the officiating over Leny Yoro's sending-off at Anfield, which dominated the build-up to this game after it was rescinded, here was another sequence of events that seemed to conspire against him.

It's not as if the Jose Alvalade Stadium was a cauldron of emotion to scramble the senses of the two sets of players and match officials either. Fernandes got a polite round of applause from the fans and a framed memento from his old club before kick-off.

When the teams came out, he was one of three former United players alongside Cristiano Ronaldo and Luis Nani honoured on a tifo of the Sporting Lisbon greats.

It has been revealed that it was all very flat until the half-hour mark when United self-imploded again. Geny Catamo picked up the ball on the edge of the United box and teased Lisandro Martinez, playing at left back.

According to recent reports, martinez took the bait and stuck his leg out. He barely caught Sporting's No 10 and it took Catamo a full second to realise he had, before going down theatrically and earning a very soft penalty from Polish referee Szymon Marciniak.

Sources indicate that sporting's top scorer Luis Suarez stepped up and made it easy for Lammens to make the save. It was a let-off for United and potentially a major moment in a difficult season for Lammens.

In a recent development, but he undid his good work 75 seconds later when Maxi Araujo chased a long ball over the top pursued by Noussair Mazraoui. For some reason, Lammens thought it would be a good idea to race 25 yards out of his goal.

Araujo stepped inside the Belgium goalkeeper and went down under his clumsy challenge. Marciniak pointed to the spot again, and this time Suarez made no mistake.

Lammens started positively saving this Luis Suarez penalty before conceding a spot-kick.

Yet, minutes later Suarez scored after being given a second penalty following Lammens error.

United thought they had eqaulised before half-time but Amad Diallo's header was ruled out for a percieved foul in the build-up by Youri Tielemans that earned him a booking.

After all the upset over the officiating at Anfield, United were on the wrong end of another big call just before half-time here when Tielemans stretched to poke the ball through to Diallo and inadvertently caught Goncalo Inacio who went down claiming serious injury.

Goalkeeper Kaique Pereira saved Diallo's first effort and Marciniak blew his whistle for a foul before the Ivorian headed in at the second attempt so there was no opportunity for VAR to review it. The referee booked Tielemans, but there was a strong argument that it wasn't even a foul.

United re-emerged for the second half undeterred and hit back to score twice through Fernandes within five minutes of the restart.

The United captain played the ball through for Martinez and then converted from the spot after his team-mate went down in a tangle of legs with Eduardo Quaresma.

Bruno Fernandes levelled for United just after half-time when they were awarded a penalty.

He then put them ahead with this left-footed shot that hit a divot on the pitch before flying in.

United's lead was undone late on when Lammens' second major error allowed Suarez to score.

United's evening was compounded when Tielemans was sent off late on for a second yellow.

According to recent reports, two minutes later, and having made the divot turning in the penalty box 17 seconds earlier, Fernandes somehow managed to hit it with a hopeful effort from 25 yards. Pereira had the ball covered but it took an outrageous deflection just outside the six-yard box and flew through his arms.

But this is United and nothing is straightforward. In the 80th minute, with victory within their grasp, Lammens had all the time in the world to catch a high ball from Ivan Fresneda. Perhaps too long. Unforgivably, he dropped it in front of Suarez who hooked into the net.

There was still time for more drama when United had another goal from a Fernandes' corner chalked off for Patrick Dorgu's foul on Pereira, after VAR sent Marciniak to the monitor, and he then demonstrated Tielemans a second yellow card.

Pochettino looked on frustrated and probably as confused as the rest of us.

#117362. An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 29m • 📚 Deep Dive (5769 w)

An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 29 min read (5769 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~29 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, over millennia, peatlands have removed hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere but emitted a proportion back as methane (CH4), exerting a slow net cooling effect1.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, over millennia, peatlands have removed hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere but emitted a proportion back as methane (CH4), exerting a slow net cooling effect1. Artificial drainage of these ecosystems—a centuries-old practice2,3—causes decomposition and the re-release of CO2 but suppresses CH4 emissions4, with a net climatic effect that is not well quantified at the global scale5. Here we reconstructed the radiative forcing from worldwide peatland drainage over 1800–2020 by combining a new flux dataset, hydrologically driven models of CO2 and CH4 fluxes and a hindcast of drainage extent and intensity. We found that drainage has produced a net heating effect of +73 (48–99) mW m−2—equivalent to 2.7 (1.8–3.6)% of industrial-era radiative forcing—originating from 0.4–0.5% of global land area. The net heating results from the dominant forcing of drainage-induced CO2 emissions (+83 (52–110) mW m−2) over that of avoided CH4 emissions (−9 (−15–−2) mW m−2). Even without further expansion of drainage, maintaining currently drained areas could almost double the cumulative warming by 2100. Our reconstruction captures the opposing impacts of peatland drainage on global budgets of CO2 and CH4 and quantifies the strong legacy effects of historical drainage on present and possibly future climate.

Newcastle United are monitoring Ajax centre-back Dies Janse as the Magpies look to strengthen their defensive options with talented young players capable of developing into long-term first-team regulars.

The 20-year-old Dutch defender has attracted interest from several Premier League clubs following his emergence in Amsterdam, with Newcastle continuing to explore opportunities in the Dutch transfer market.

However, Ajax’s determination to retain one of their brightest defensive prospects could complicate any potential move.

According to TEAMtalk, Newcastle are among four Premier League clubs monitoring Janse’s development.

The Netherlands Under-21 international is comfortable operating as a left-sided centre-back or left-back, making his versatility particularly attractive to potential suitors.

Janse spent the 2025/26 campaign on loan at FC Groningen, scoring twice in 31 league appearances before returning to Ajax, where he has since made 15 senior appearances.

Ajax extended his contract until June 2030 in September following growing interest from clubs across Europe.

Newcastle have already established a connection with the Dutch market, having signed midfielder Sean Steur from Ajax for £23million during the summer.

A separate NUFC Blog report also highlights Newcastle’s interest in fellow Ajax defender Aaron Bouwman, suggesting the Magpies are exploring multiple options to strengthen their defensive ranks.

Newcastle’s interest in Janse makes considerable sense from a squad-building perspective.

Recruiting promising young defenders before their valuations increase significantly could help the club remain competitive while maintaining financial flexibility.

His ability to cover two defensive positions would also provide useful tactical options, particularly during demanding periods of the season.

There are similarities with Newcastle’s successful recruitment of Sven Botman, another defender who developed through Ajax’s academy before establishing himself elsewhere.

However, Janse is still relatively inexperienced, and Newcastle should not expect him to become an immediate Premier League regular.

Ajax’s strong contractual position also means negotiations are unlikely to be straightforward.

Rather than forcing through a January transfer, Newcastle would be better served by monitoring his performances throughout the remainder of the campaign.

If Janse continues progressing at his current rate, a summer move could represent another intelligent investment in Newcastle’s long-term defensive future.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leeds United have triggered a club option to extend Lukas Nmecha's contract at Elland Road.

Nmecha, 27, joined the Whites on a free transfer in June 2025, following his departure from Wolfsburg. He penned a two-year deal in West Yorkshire and scored on his debut in a 1-0 win against Everton.

Industry observers note that but the German had to wait three months to find the net again, when he struck in a 3-1 defeat at Nottingham Forest. That started a mini purple patch for Nmecha, who netted in three successive matches and became Daniel Farke's first-choice striker, replacing Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

According to recent reports, however, that is as good as it has got for Nmecha in a Leeds shirt. After suffering a hamstring injury, he lost his place in the starting line-up back to Calvert-Lewin and the ex-Everton man hasn't looked back since, cementing himself as Farke's main man up front.

GIVEMESPORT exclusively revealed on Tuesday that Calvert-Lewin was set to sign a latest contract himself, as he becomes the Yorkshire outfit's talisman.

It has left Nmecha as back-up, and with Calvert-Lewin starting all 11 Premier League matches this season, he has had to make do with appearances on the left and in the No.10.

Indeed, Nmecha started the 1-0 win against Tottenham earlier this month as one of the two attacking midfielders alongside Sean Longstaff. But after struggling, he dropped down to the bench for the trip to Chelsea on Saturday, a game the Whites ended up winning 4-1.

Noah Okafor, who replaced Nmecha in the XI, scored twice as Leeds moved up to seventh in the Premier League table and fans are now believing a European push could be on.

Despite the fact Nmecha is not in Farke's best starting side, Leeds do not want to lose him. And now, according to The Athletic, the final formalities are being concluded on a one-year contract extension for Nmecha after the Whites triggered an option in his current deal.

Nmecha was due to be out of contract at the end of the season, but he will be tied down until 2028 once the paperwork is finalised, ensuring he is still at Leeds for at least another 18 months.

While some Leeds fans are a little frustrated that the club have triggered the extension on Nmecha's contract, given the fact he hasn't scored since February and has struggled this season, he is still an important squad player and will be a cost-effective option if the Whites secure European football.

Leeds will need a bigger squad if they reach Europe, and given Nmecha's experience on the continent in Belgium and Germany, he could be crucial for Farke in that competition.

Recent findings suggest that as well as that, he is one of the lowest earners in the first-team squad at £45,000 per-week and there isn't too many better players Leeds can replace him with who would take that wage and join on a free transfer. For me, it's a no-brainer to extend Nmecha's contract.

Alongside the fact he could be notable for Leeds if they secure European football, the extension to Nmecha's deal also protects his value and means the Whites could sell him to make profit.

Recent findings suggest that and should Leeds fail to make Europe, that is the option they should take. Selling Nmecha in those circumstances would make sense, as it's clear he is not good enough for a regular spot in the Premier League XI but can cut it in the Europa League or Conference League, for sure.

Industry observers note that nmecha can still make an impact from the bench and even in the FA Cup for Leeds this season. He set up Calvert-Lewin's equaliser in the draw against Brentford in August and has shown that he can influence matches when needed, even if he isn't as effective as the likes of Okafor.
