📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, NEWLY INTRODUCED YORK – The awkward logistics of Sunday's NWSL semifinal at Icahn Stadium, a quirky little venue sandwiched on an island in between Manhattan and Queens, were supposed to give way once Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current took to the pitch for one of the league's showpiece matches. When the Current's Croix Bethune opened the scoring in the 20th minute with an incredible looping shot off a free kick, the theme of the day was in motion. The league would make the best of the unideal circumstances with a top-quality soccer game, or at least with a few highlight-reel moments nestled into a match contested by a collection of the world's most talented players.

"I've been working on free kicks all year," Bethune noted post-match, the Current justified in their decision to sign her last winter even if the validation was no longer needed, "and a lot more leading into the playoffs so just practice makes perfect.".

Icahn Stadium's irregularities, though, seemed to reflect the game it unexpectedly became the host of six days earlier. The Current's 2-1 win came courtesy of a chippy game proposal that would have been the case if the match had taken place at a traditional soccer-specific stadium but it felt especially at home at Icahn Stadium and amidst its elements. The teams played against the wind during Upcoming York's first properly cold weekend of the season, and Gotham faced a setting sun that impacted their vision during the first half. Bethune's impressive strike was really the only on-field spectacle to be witnessed on Randall's Island.

BEND IT LIKE BETHUNE 💫 KC takes the lead!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/F4mQePT5QJ.

"We knew it was going to be a physical game, without a doubt," Current forward Haley Hopkins stated. "Like I said a million times, Gotham's a very, very good team and so we had to be super disciplined in our structure and catch them on their transition and we were just able to put the ball in the back of the net when we had our opportunities.".

It has been revealed that the introduction of Gotham's Rose Lavelle, who has been dealing with niggling fitness problems over the last few weeks, did not change the smash-and-grab energy of the game. Much as there was a week ago in their quarterfinal win over the Seattle Reign, there was a dull quality to Gotham's attack despite their star power. Over 180 minutes of possession play, the NWSL Shield winners managed zero shots on target and 0.66 expected goals, their midseason marquee signing Sam Kerr managing no shots along the way and mustering just one attempt in her last five matches. To say they were unlucky would be a stretch but their lively start to the second half gave their failed attempts to put a shot on frame a comedic feel.

In a recent development, "I think we were kind of our own worst enemy today," midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. "I think at times we played into what they wanted to do and their style of play. They want a very chippy game. They want to get into tackles. They want to draw fouls. They want to break up the game. They want to play long and that's not our style. We want to keep the ball. We want to control tempo, and we like to play pretty football. That's [what] we pride ourselves on … but I think we need to find a better way to balance that out, especially in this league. How can we meet the demand of a chippy game while also controlling the tempo? I think we did a really good job when we played them at home the last time [a 2-1 win on Aug. 14]. They scored early but then we completely dominated the rest of the game and I think we failed to do that today and so I think that's really the determining factor.".

It has been revealed that in other words, it was the perfect setup for Gotham to equalize off an own goal from Laney Rouse, a week after benefiting from another own goal from the Reign's Jordyn Bugg. Those two goals would be the only ones in their postseason run, just as one might expect from the NWSL Shield winners and reigning champions who entered the playoffs as the favorites to win another title.

Gotham FC find a way to tie up the semifinal 💪NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/Itbzs4Bhz1.

It has been revealed that gotham goalkeeper Ann-Katrin Berger then slipped into game-saving mode with two vital blocks while defender Tierna Davidson did what she could to hold the Current at bay, attempting to create a villain arc rivaled only by Argentina's run to the World Cup final. Though the hosts had lucked their way into an even game by the 88th minute, the dark and cold conditions at a downsized stadium in an obscure part of Latest York meant the game beckoned for extra time. One final smash and grab was undoubtedly in the cards, though where it would come from was hard to guess – the Current had put in the work to win but soccer's chaotic nature had already weaseled its way into the game.

Industry observers note that in the end, it was the Current's Haley Hopkins who had the final say in the 89th minute off of – what else – a set piece, a free kick that led the forward to finally evade Berger with a shot off the crossbar. After losing to them twice in three previous meetings this season, the Current earned their spot in next week's NWSL Championship (Saturday, 8 p.m. ET, CBS, Paramount+) on the back of a well-executed gameplan.

HALEY HOPKINS CLUTCH OFF THE CROSSBAR 🤯The KC Current lead 2-1!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/BT2OZhwX1y.

"As much as we tried to analyze certain teams in the league that have given them trouble, we really took information from the games we've played against them, all the ways they challenged us," Current head coach Chris Armas stated. "There's been games even where they get high [expected goals], too much progression, too much in our box and we just tried to then look at all the scenes and moments when we made it hard for them so we just tried to take from yesterday and apply it to today, [that] type of thing. We gave up zero shots on goal in 90 minutes. The commitment from our players to just will themselves to it to stick to a match blueprint that was going to be largely about taking away spaces, controlling the middle of the pitch and if we can do that on the day – and and we did that by running after them, too, and pressing in moments of high intensity – we not only might stop what they're trying to do on one end and maybe force the turnovers that could challenge them so a little bit of a chess match there in moments.".

Recent findings suggest that the Current were no slouches, finishing fourth in the regular season and now on a  seven-game winning streak en route to next week's championship. Bethune's star quality shone on Sunday, while the team's record with two-time NWSL MVP Temwa Chawinga and U.S. women's national team standout Michelle Cooper is formidable. It did not erase the fact that they slayed a giant along the way, knocking out the Shield winners and a team that had picked up five major titles in four seasons.

In a recent development, "Gotham has just raised the bar around the league and in our country here, so the way they play, the way the coach sets them up, the talent on the team, the type of games they can put you in, you have to come with a blueprint," Armas noted. "They're a team that, again, if iron sharpens iron type of thing, we try to push teams and we try to raise the bar.".

According to recent reports, gotham, though, had not looked the part of the NWSL's gold standard team. Their drastic run, while at the moment headlined by USWNT players Lavelle and Jaedyn Shaw, is built on the back of an effective defensive structure that has carried an inconsistent offense. Lavelle and, in particular, Shaw have picked up much of the slack en route to the NWSL Shield and Kerr was supposed to bolster their attack after Esther Gonzalez's shock departure for Saudi club Al Qadsiah. They finished the regular season sixth in the NWSL for expected goals with 49.01 but had a genuine finishing problem, notching just 39 goals and ranking in the league's bottom six in that category. Head coach Juan Carlos Amoros is not sounding the alarm just yet but as they enter another offseason, the attacking composition of the team deserves yet another look.

"Of course, we want to create more chances, more shots," Amoros remarked. "We all do but we look at the way we play. We look at the way we create chances. We look at who does that. I think when it comes to these games, could we have [made] some better decisions? Yes, we did. We actually create some good moments. Yes, I wouldn't over-think about it. Something that I'm happy [about]? No but at the same time, we work a lot to make sure that those moments happen. So you know the set pieces, those situations, the open plays, final decisions … Definitely, something that we want to be better [at]. We want to score more goals. I think that we are the best team defending in the league with our aggressive approach to defending but we want to also be able to create and score more goals.".

It has been revealed that more importantly, though, Gotham were not treated like the bar-raising team they have become over the years. Icahn Stadium has its charms and is a worthy inclusion on the list of wacky and wonderful places that embody American soccer, an enjoyably chaotic slice of the world's most popular game. It was also a back-up plan for a team that has called Sports Illustrated Stadium home for five years, settling in nicely to a state-of-the-art soccer-specific build for MLS' Red Bull Upcoming York that can hold 20,000 more fans than the 5,000-seater Icahn Stadium can. The pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium, managed by RBNY, had fallen into disrepair and with the primary tenants' end-of-season friendly scheduled for the night before, there was not enough time to fix it. The quirks of Icahn Stadium only served as a reminder that Gotham – and the NWSL – should not have actually been there, even if the field at Randall's Island was better suited for the occasion.

"I want to be really clear and direct in saying that in these types of situations, the field is never an excuse," winger Midge Purce noted. "We lost today because we weren't the better team. That being said, I would say it's inexcusable. It's not what you want in a professional league. It's not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it's a bad look for everyone involved and we always want to be at Sports Illustrated [Stadium] in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season but I would say it had no effect on performance today.".

It has been revealed that the Current's trip to Icahn Stadium is not where the NWSL's efforts to make lemonade end, either. Saturday's semifinal, in which the Washington Spirit beat the Utah Royals to book their spot in a championship game at their home of Audi Field, only added to it. One of the Spirit's sponsors underwrote the costs to push the start time of the Secretaries' Cup, a Division III football game, by a few hours but both matches were played on a field with soccer and football lines. The football lines will likely be faint but visible for next week's NWSL Championship, while the playability of the actual field will probably face a few questions in the build-up.

"I think we will never know what happened if we would have played [at Sports Illustrated Stadium] on a good pitch," Amoros stated. "I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable under our view. The last couple of games we picked up injuries. Luckily, nothing that has been a season-ending injury but we have to protect our players and guarantee the quality of football so to thank the club, obviously.

It has been revealed that "Overall, I think it's been a sad weekend. I think also the situation in Washington yesterday. This league deserves better. The two, arguably, best teams, [most] consistent, having to deal with these situations and then yesterday, you sit down to watch that game around the world and you're seeing those American football lines across today. Credit to the club and the fans. I think they've done an amazing job here. The fans welcomed us. The club has really shifted everything to play here but we couldn't play in our ground where we could have had more people, where we are unbeaten in 13 games at the moment and but I think we took that decision, putting players' safety first, and the outcome is the outcome.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Inter managed to get the better of VfB Stuttgart and leapfrog them in the Champions League table thanks to Petar Sucic and Lautaro Martinez.

The Nerazzurri lost their first two Champions League games, then won back-to-back against Shakhtar Donetsk and Feyenoord. Hakan Calhanoglu and Ange-Yoan Bonny missed out, with Lautaro Martinez only fit for the bench after more than a month on the sidelines. Manuel Akanji returned in defence after Sunday’s chaotic 4-4 Serie A draw away to Atalanta.

VfB Stuttgart were one point in front of Inter going into this clash, with Angelo Stiller, Leo Sauer and Luca Jacquez back in the squad after injury.

See how it all unfolded on the Liveblog.

It was an aggressive start from the Germans, as Maximilian Mittelstadt flashed a ball across the face of goal from the left, then Petar Sucic charged down the Ermedin Demirovic strike.

Josep Martinez needed a big save to deny the ferocious Chris Fuhrich strike at the near post, while Djed Spence wasted a very promising counter-attack from the centre-circle, firing straight at the on-rushing goalkeeper.

Inter threatened from a corner, flicked on by Yann Bisseck just beyond both Pio Esposito and Manuel Akanji, and another of the defender’s headers on a set play was charged down.

A well-worked move fell apart when Henrikh Mkhitaryan’s first touch let him down meeting the Marcus Thuram roll across from the left, while Ramon Hendriks had to make a perfect tackle on Spence inside the area.

Industry observers note that finishing from Bisseck and Sucic left something to be desired, but Inter were forced into a change when Alessandro Bastoni limped off with a left thigh injury. Federico Dimarco came on, moving Carlos Augusto to central defence.

Sources indicate that the hosts had two huge chances to score in the space of three minutes. First, Marcus Thuram ran onto a misplaced pass only to drill it wide of the near post, then Barella’s curler off the outside of the boot bounced off the upright and Dennis Seimen clawed the rebound off the line.

Thuram also saw his strike deflected over the bar, but Nartey blasted just over from the edge of the area after the restart.

There was finally a breakthrough when Vagnoman charged down the Dimarco cross with a raised arm, spotted by VAR, and Petar Sucic kept his cool to convert the penalty.

VfB threatened from a corner kick, Bisseck getting himself in the way of the Nartey effort from point-blank range, while at the other end Dimarco’s deflected free kick was acrobatically palmed out from under the crossbar.

Carlos Augusto made a desperate interception to prevent Demirovic turning in at the back post, while Jamie Leweling’s curler was just over.

However, Inter doubled their lead when Pio Esposito let the Dimarco cross through with a dummy, allowing Lautaro Martinez to take a touch and fire in with the right foot.

Akanji also required a crucial block as Bilal El Khannouss burst into the box and got the shot away, while in stoppages Lautaro Martinez’s strike was charged down by a defender’s face.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A court in Asturias has convicted the Real Oviedo supporter who made monkey gestures at Kylian Mbappé of a hate crime. The case adds to a growing list of criminal convictions for racist abuse of Real Madrid players in Spanish grounds.

The Real Oviedo supporter who racially abused Kylian Mbappé at the Carlos Tartiere has been convicted of a hate crime. The Second Section of the Audiencia Provincial de Asturias delivered the verdict on 17 November 2026. It was a verdict by agreement, known in Spain as conformidad.

According to recent reports, the abuse came during Real Oviedo v Real Madrid on 24 August 2025. The fan made monkey gestures and noises in the 37th minute. Real Madrid’s players were celebrating Mbappé’s opening goal at the time.

Sources indicate that the man will not go to prison as long as he keeps to the terms of his sentence. The term is suspended on condition that he stays away from football stadiums hosting official competitions for two years, Real Madrid remarked in an official statement. The prosecuting parties also tied the suspension to a ban from LaLiga stadiums and a ban on approaching Mbappé. The defendant accepted these conditions.

Recent findings suggest that the fine was set at six months at a daily rate of €8. He is also barred from working in education, teaching, sport or leisure for three years and 11 months.

The case was charged under article 510.2.a of the Spanish Criminal Code. LaLiga filed the original complaint. It also supplied expert lip-reading evidence that proved key to resolving the case. Real Madrid later joined the proceedings as a private prosecutor.

The ruling is LaLiga’s twelfth conviction for racism in Spanish football, Servimedia reported. The league presented the outcome as proof of its commitment to fighting racism.

The Carlos Tartiere has featured in this list before. In April 2026, a supporter was convicted over abuse of Marcus Rashford at Real Oviedo v FC Barcelona. That person received a nine-month prison sentence. Another conviction, handed down in September 2025, followed abuse of Iñaki Williams at an Espanyol v Athletic Club match from the 2019/20 season.

For Real Madrid, the verdict extends a run of cases involving its own players. The club has listed earlier convictions for racist abuse at Mestalla, Son Moix, Vallecas and the José Zorrilla. The Valladolid case ended on 21 May 2025. The Audiencia Provincial de Valladolid convicted five people of hate crimes for abusing Vinícius Júnior at the José Zorrilla on 30 December 2022. Each received a one-year prison sentence.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that three days after tearing up as he revealed his departure from the U.S.
  • After two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity.
  • It has been revealed that "For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he said on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that three days after tearing up as he revealed his departure from the U.S. men's national team, outgoing head coach Mauricio Pochettino said he does not want to think about the emotions that will hit him once the job comes to an end with Tuesday's Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti. He preached that it's still business as usual, even as one unusual week comes to a close and another equally unusual week begins.

After two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity. The task in front of them on Tuesday is a simple one, especially after Saturday's 6-0 win over Haiti in the first leg – play like Pochettino's version of the U.S. team one last time.

It has been revealed that "For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he said on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England. "I don't want to be disappointed. I don't want to lose the focus. I don't want to be less concentrated … [If] you take the game in a way that claims it's not crucial tomorrow because it's already done, I think you will pay in the future – that lack of respect to the competition, to the opponent, to the result, to yourself. That is why tomorrow what I want is I'm going to put the best team possible and to perform.".

Pochettino has been hesitant to reflect on his legacy after two years with the USMNT but that has been a common refrain during his tenure, spending just as much time molding the team's mentality in his image as he has their style of play. He leaves behind a mixed track record – results were all over the place in the build-up to the World Cup but it all appeared to come together once the tournament started, only for the U.S. team to fall flat on their faces in a round of 16 exit forever tinged by the Folarin Balogun affair. The stakes are undoubtedly lower against Haiti, the first leg advantage so substantial that the USMNT can probably survive another unimpressive performance before closing the book on the Pochettino years. There's a hint of succession planning in his plans for Tuesday, though, even if those plans are no longer his to execute.

According to recent reports, "What I hope is to create the same link with us, with the new coaches that arrive here," Pochettino said. "It's to create the same link with the players. [It's] become an emotional relationship, that you can find the best for this group of players that have enormous talent … That is an official game and it's the opportunity to keep growing for the future, to settle all the principles and grow and grow and grow.".

For all his faults and shortcomings, Pochettino does leave the national team in better shape than he found it. Some of it is out of his control – up and comers like Julian Hall, who scored on Saturday and now has four goals in his first five games for the senior team, were very likely poised for success no matter who the USMNT head coach was. After much trial and tribulation, though, he implemented a clear style of play and a cultural shift that several players have championed over the last week. Tuesday's game is ultimately a showcase for the players who will remain long after Pochettino leaves, both on an individual level as they aim to impress whoever takes the helm and as they try to prove a collective point now that the Pochettino years are over. U.S. Soccer's financial might may help sway Pochettino's eventual successor to take the job, no matter who that might be, but there is a pure soccer argument to taking this job.

For perhaps the first time in its modern history, the USMNT can prioritize style of play with their next hire. That's true outside the reported approach for ex-Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola, whose interest in the job is unclear. Pochettino's high-intensity, attack-minded version of the U.S. team suited the players at this year's World Cup and feels especially tailor-made for the rising talents headlined by Cavan Sullivan, the 17-year-old Philadelphia Union attacker who is now MLS' youngest-ever MVP nominee. A strong outing on Tuesday will allow the Pochettino years to look like a stepping stone to an crucial newly introduced chapter, one that will hopefully get the best out of the experienced players as well as their younger teammates, no matter who oversees the project.

As for Pochettino, laying the groundwork for the USMNT's future comes while he focuses on his own. Assistant coach Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez and sports scientist Sebastiano Pochettino departed for Manchester after Saturday's win over Haiti at Miami's Nu Stadium, filling in the gaps before Pochettino departs Cincinnati on Wednesday to begin his upcoming role. The rest of his coaching staff will stay in Ohio to finish out the international break with the USMNT before traveling alongside Pochettino.

Two years removed from starting a newly introduced job with a short runway, Pochettino will do so again at United. The earliest he can oversee his first training session with United is Thursday, three days before an all-crucial clash with Liverpool. The longtime London resident, who previously coached Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea, insists he will not be out of the loop when he finally makes his Premier League return.

Industry observers note that "For me, it's not difficult," he noted of the quick turnaround. "I think we are well prepared to switch quick to like a player, from the national team to the clubs, from one game that you don't play well to another that you need to be ready again, from one action to the next action. I think we are well-prepared and then all the experience from the past, I think, helps us to be focused in the priority of the moment that demands that business. Today is to be focusing here in Cincinnati for the game against Haiti tomorrow but for sure, in the moment that game [finishes], we are going to start to be 100% focused in our next project … We watch soccer every day, all the leagues and we are always because that is our passion, our passion. We know the team [very well]. We know every single team [very well] and I think we don't need to match the preparation about the opponent. The most notable [thing] is to know the details about our players, our staff, our culture, our identity and from there, to improve but now we are focusing [on] that game and we want to finish well tomorrow.".

A large task awaits Pochettino at United, who are currently in the relegation zone with just one win from their opening 10 league games of the season.

Industry News: Klopp and Wirtz offer glimpse of bright German future

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Despite a patchy start to his reign, Klopp's relentless positivity towards a group of Germany players not viewed in the most flattering light outside the squad has been rewarded.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Extraordinary," "Insane," "Magnificent," "A special group." Even by Jürgen Klopp's effusive standards, Germany's 5-0 win over rivals the Netherlands on Monday was clearly pleasing.

Despite a patchy start to his reign, Klopp's relentless positivity towards a group of Germany players not viewed in the most flattering light outside the squad has been rewarded.

"Everyone will go home with a smile on their face, and for at least the next three or four months, no one will be questioning the German national team," Klopp told German public broadcaster ARD, referencing that Germany will not play again until the end of March 2027.

Recent findings suggest that "Instead, they'll be thinking: 'This could really turn into something. We have wonderful footballers, great characters," Klopp remarked, and added: "The lads are even surprising themselves.".

In a recent development, the former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund coach took the job in July after Julian Nagelsmann paid the price for another German early World Cup exit, this time to Paraguay in the last 32. Klopp always preached patience, particularly after his first two matches yielded a fortunate 1-1 draw with the Netherlands and a 1-0 home loss to Greece.

It paid off on Monday as Germany performed with the hallmarks of Klopp's great club sides — fierce pressing, intensity, pace and a measure of joy. Perhaps it is in Florian Wirtz that Klopp's impact is more notable.

Recent findings suggest that the 23-year-old has struggled to make a significant impact at Liverpool since moving to the Premier League from Bayer Leverkusen at the beginning of last season. But he has four goals in his last four games for Germany and is demonstrating the ability that earned him a €125 million ($137.5 million) move to England.

In a recent development, "I only knew him from television. I was shocked when I saw him on the pitch for the first time. An extraordinary footballer," Klopp mentioned after the Netherlands match.

"We've also found the right position for Flo. It helps that he's so vocal. He's the first pressing player, he can press two players without getting tired.".

That quality was evident in Wirtz's first goal on Monday, when he won back possession on the edge of the Dutch box before combining some dazzling footwork with a brilliant, curled finish.

Sources indicate that but Wirtz wasn't the only attacking bright spot for Germany. Rookie wingers Derry Scherhant and Brajan Gruda both scored and were a huge threat throughout. Klopp gave debuts to both earlier this year as he sought to spread opportunities. The pair have offered Germany a pace they often lacked under Naglesmann and his predecessor Hansi Flick.

"They can both play, my goodness," said Klopp.

Sources indicate that scherhant, who opened the scoring with another stunning strike, spent many days of his boyhood on the terraces of the Olympiastadion in Berlin, where Monday's game was played. Unlike many pros, he bounced about Berlin's lower league clubs as a youth before Hertha Berlin signed him up. He then moved to Freiburg in 2025 and is rapidly emerging as a player who can implement Klopp's style and reflect the coach's attitude.

"A few years ago, people told me I wouldn't make it as a pro. Then I became a pro. And even then, some people still mentioned it wasn't enough—that the Regionalliga (Germany's fourth tier) was the best I could hope for,” Scherhant said.

"It's just unbelievable that I get to stand here now with the satisfaction of having proven those people wrong.".

Proving people wrong is also a major part of Klopp's remit. After failing to get beyond the quarterfinal of a major tournament since 2016, the German public's interest in and enthusiasm for its men's national team had waned. Klopp's mission he mentioned, was to "to prove to Germany and the world that we can play soccer.".

While that was achieved on Monday, the loss (and subsequent 0-0 draw) against Greece in the Nations League game were evidence that it won't all be plain sailing. Indeed, Germany have had plenty of false dawns of late, as captain Joshua Kimmich alluded to.

"We've been through a tough time," he said. "A clear victory doesn't make all that go away," he added before saying that the task was to "turn potential into quality and a team that's all about 'what ifs' into a team that's all about 'reality.' That's the art of it.".

Klopp too, for all his hype, was keen not to get too far ahead of himself.

"We want to gradually solidify it. We're not done yet. We still have a few areas to work on. But I'm looking forward to our future — it's crazy what's still to come," he said.

In Nations League terms, that will be a matchup with world champions Spain, or Portugal or Belgium before qualifying for Euro 2028 begins. For now though, Klopp and his players can enjoy some time with those smiles on their faces.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United did not just lose to Everton, they lost the home crowd, whose enthusiasm to back their team has drained from them at alarming speed.

Recent findings suggest that this was a performance that belonged in the pre-takeover era, those bad old days under Steve McClaren, John Carver and Steve Bruce. It was a hugely satisfying evening for Everton manager David Moyes, who insisted there was “a way back” for Jack Grealish, even though he was once again left at home after he missed training last week without permission.

The atmosphere went flat early and gradually turned into anger and frustration. The crowd initially tried to stay with their team but were repeatedly punched in the face by the grim reality of the spectacle in front of them. They do not like the style of play, they do not like the application of the players and they cannot accept the results. They are fed up with pretending otherwise.

This was another miserable performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side, who did not manage a shot on target until the 86th minute. He has only been in the job three months, but nothing seems to be getting better.

According to recent reports, “I have to take the responsibility,” he noted. “We did not transfer the things we did in training. Hitting long balls all the time, that was not the initiative. We were not brave enough to play short passes.

In a recent development, “As soon as the referee blew his whistle, the strategy disappeared. We could feel the anger and the frustration, I felt it on the touchline. We are low on confidence and it indicates.”.

Sources indicate that newcastle looked listless, clueless and alarmingly devoid of belief in what they were being asked to do. They have the unmistakable whiff of a team in decline.

It has been revealed that if they do not start playing a lot better, they will be worried about a relegation battle. It is four defeats in their last five games and the confidence in Jaissle to find solutions is fading. Rather than change what he is asking his team to do, he has doubled down on the formation and tactics.

Concerns have been creeping steadily upwards since August. There is a lack of confidence in the players, and worries about the quality of the eight new signings made over the summer.

In particular, there are serious misgivings about the implementation of the “vertical football” Jaissle has imported to the North East of England from the Austro-German Red Bull coaching school.

A night under the lights at St James’ Park should be a boisterous affair, but things went flat promptly. Newcastle, as they have tended to do this season, resorted to long balls punted forward. More often than not they were poorly directed – only 22 per cent were accurate over 98 minutes.

Sources indicate that there was no fluency and no threat. The first groans were heard inside 15 minutes as another pass was hoisted harmlessly into the air. They grew more widespread and more frequent.

Sources indicate that everton, just as they had in their Carabao Cup win last week, looked comfortable. Recognising how easy it was to nullify Newcastle’s game initiative, they offered an attacking threat of their own.

A rising shot from Merlin Röhl briefly had goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek worried. A free-kick into the Newcastle box caused panic. James Tarkowski won the first header, but Thierno Barry swung and missed with his left foot.

Recent findings suggest that the groans began to turn into boos and whistles. Jaissle’s side could barely string more than two passes together. It felt precarious.

Industry observers note that this is not an easy place to play football when the crowd airs its displeasure. As the first half limped on, there were players in black and white who looked like they could not handle the pressure.

In a recent development, it was a horrible game of football. With the last kick of the half, Everton should have taken the lead, Harrison Armstrong picked out Barry inside the box, but he made a mess of the finish. The referee’s whistle was accompanied by boos and a scream of “sort it out” from behind Jaissle’s technical area.

He did not follow those blunt instructions. Everton took the lead in such simple fashion and all Jaissle and his coaching staff could do was shake their heads at each other. Industry observers note that newcastle and Everton meet for the second time in matter of days as the Premier League weekend concludes in the north east at St James’ Park. These teams encountered each other on Thursday night in the League Cup, where Everton won 3-1 at the Hill Dickinson to progress to the quarter-finals in that competition.

Sources indicate that newcastle, who won 2-0 at Crystal Palace in their last league outing, come into this game in 12th, with the chance to rise to seventh with a victory tonight. Their boss Matthias Jaissle has called on his players to use the defeat against Everton on Thursday as fuel for tonight.

Sources indicate that “Now it is about taking that frustration into motivation for Monday and having that approach for the rematch,” Jaissle stated. “We take it as a long-term journey, and our approach is to make progress, to see improvements. Now it is time to learn fast out of the mistakes that we just did. [There are] other phases where we can already see that we improved and this is something we can count on, we can build on, the good part. But football is also in the end about results so you need to avoid these simple mistakes.”.

Everton, who have not won in the league since a 1-0 victory over Ipswich back in September, begin the night in 14th but, like Newcastle, could rise to seventh with a win. There are just two points that separate Bournemouth in seventh and Everton in 14th. Despite getting the better of Newcastle the other night, Everton manager David Moyes has warned that game will count for nothing tonight.

Recent findings suggest that “It is a different ball game,” Moyes stated. “Go to St James’ Park, on a Monday evening, they will get a crowd up there, you always know you are up against it. But we will go with confidence. We have played Newcastle a couple of times this year and done well, so we have to try and continue it. But Newcastle have got some really, really good players and players you have to concern yourself about.”.

Jack Grealish was left out of Everton’s squad for that League Cup victory because of an unauthorised absence from training and the 31-year-old is not expected to be involved tonight.

Sources indicate that these sides were involved in a dramatic fixture on this ground last season. Everton claimed a 3-2 victory, with Thierno Barry earning them all three points in the 83rd minute, moments after Jacob Murphy had equalised for Newcastle. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 04:25 EST, 22 November 2026.

When Mauricio Pochettino boarded a flight from London to Atlanta a little over two weeks ago, there was little indication that by the time he landed back in the UK it would be as the newly introduced head coach of Manchester United.

The club were aware of the £7.5million buyout clause in his contract with the US national team as they began to consider potential replacements for Michael Carrick, but it hadn’t gone any further than that.

According to recent reports, however, United’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on October 25 left Carrick’s job hanging by a thread. He was given a two-week stay of execution that also allowed United time to step up their search for a suitable replacement.

At a meeting of the club’s executive committee on November 5 – after United had lost to Chelsea and staged a chaotic Champions League win against Roma – it was decided that Pochettino would be the No.1 choice if Carrick was sacked.

By the time the Argentine caught that flight to Atlanta 24 hours later to take charge of the USA's two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Haiti, United were preparing to make their move.

This is the story of the whirlwind two weeks that will end with Pochettino taking charge of his first game as United boss against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday following the dramatic events on both sides of the Atlantic.

Industry observers note that patrick Dorgu’s injury-time header rescued United from another defeat as they snatched a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford, but it wasn’t enough to save Carrick. His fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp.

There is a five-hour time difference between Manchester and Georgia, so it was late afternoon when Pochettino first learned of United’s interest at the Trilith Guesthouse – close to the US national team’s training base in Fayetteville south-west of Atlanta – as the players began to report there for duty.

Michael Carrick's fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp after the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford.

As speculation raged over Carrick’s future, the odds on Pochettino replacing him at Old Trafford were slashed after some substantial money was placed on the 54-year-old overnight.

Recent findings suggest that preliminary talks continued with his representatives who made the US Soccer Federation aware of the situation. Pochettino discussed it over dinner at the team hotel with chief executive JT Batson and chief operating officer Dan Helfrich who knew it was pointless trying to change his mind.

‘That was the big day,’ notes a source close to Pochettino, who took US team training in Fayetteville. ‘It became real and the optimism grew.’.

As talks accelerated between United and their prospective latest head coach, Carrick returned to Carrington to work with the United players not on international duty while chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew to Monaco to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and rubber-stamp the change.

United reached verbal agreement with Pochettino over a two-and-a-half-year deal, and agreed to pay US Soccer around £10million to buy the 54-year-old and his staff – No 2 Jesus Perez, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino (Mauricio’s son), strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott – out of their contracts.

Industry observers note that there was never any question of him leaving before the two Haiti ties, even though it left little time before his first game against Liverpool. Pochettino is said to have been respectful of the USA’s position and felt an obligation to see the job through.

As a compromise, it was agreed that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr would be allowed to leave for Manchester after the first leg regardless of the result.

Industry observers note that media in the US were informed that access to the players had been cancelled out of respect for Veterans Day. It also meant that they don’t have to answer questions about Pochettino’s future.

Carrick returned to Carrington at 7.50am for the last time as United head coach and was sacked in a meeting with Berrada and Wilcox.

By the time Pochettino woke up in Fayetteville, United officially had a managerial vacancy and he gathered the players together for a scheduled team briefing at 10am.

Pochettino went through the usual pre-match preparation, and then invited staff into the room for the second half of the meeting.

There was some emotion but no surprise when he informed them of his decision to take the United job. ‘As you’d expect, he spoke from the heart,’ says a source. ‘He loved being here but United was a dream opportunity. It was too hard to say no, but hard to say goodbye.’.

United officially announced Pochettino’s appointment and confirmed that he would stay in charge for the USA’s two games against Haiti before starting work the following Wednesday.

Pochettino conducted his pre-match press conference in Fayetteville, flanked by CEO chief JT Batson and president Cindy Parlow Cone, and broke down in tears as he thanked them for their support over the last 26 months.

Otherwise, the preparation is remarked to have gone according to plan as the US squad flew to Miami.

The Argentine broke down in tears as he thanked the USA for their support over the last 26 months.

According to recent reports, the US smashed Haiti 6-0 to all but guarantee their place in the semi-finals. Even so the message from Pochettino to his players after the game was: ‘This tie isn’t over.’.

The players learned for the first time that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr were leaving camp, and they headed straight to Manchester.

Pochettino flew with the players from Miami to Cincinnati for the second leg at the TQL Stadium.

On a visit to the Kenwood Towne Centre shopping mall, a man whose profile had risen in the US during his two years in charge of the national team was approached by even more fans than normal.

When Pochettino appeared as a guest of honour at the NFL game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium that night, a number of Bengals’ players and staff congratulated him on his upcoming job claiming to be United fans.

It emerged that United had provided a private jet for Pochettino and the remainder of his staff to fly straight from Cincinnati to Manchester through the night after the second leg.

In his pre-match press conference, he confirmed the departure of his three coaches over the weekend, and it was no surprise to learn that he was in constant contact over several days as he prepared to join them at Carrington.

The US beat Haiti by two goals to complete an 8-0 aggregate win. Afterwards, they played Take Me Home, Country Roads by John Denver over the stadium PA, which has been a tradition since the US hosted the World Cup last summer but carried particular poignance given that it has also been adopted as an anthem at United.

Pochettino invited all the staff onto the pitch for a team photo as he led a chant of U-S-A, and there was a tearful send-off in the dressing-room as he was presented with a signed shirt and a special hand-painted bottle of Clase Azul tequila.

It’s a favourite tipple of Pochettino’s and staff also ordered food from Chick-fil-A, which Pochettino regrets won’t be available in Manchester.

He never had a permanent residence in America, so he left the stadium at 10.30pm with the same suitcase he had brought from London and headed for Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport for the flight to Manchester.

Pochettino had a poor night’s sleep before landing shortly before noon aboard the grey Gulfstream G700 jet with D’Agostino, Scott and Tuya.

He posted a picture from the skies above Manchester and was then driven to Carrington, changing into an official United tracksuit en route.

Pochettino was too late for training but met with some of the players and club executives before being given a tour of the training ground and conducting an interview with MUTV which wrapped up about 7pm. He stayed at the training ground long into the evening to catch up on his preparation for Liverpool.

The plane believed to be carrying Pochettino and his staff was hired by Manchester United.

Industry observers note that more players returned from international duty, but Pochettino’s first training session with them at Carrington was ambushed by a drone shooting video footage that was posted online. It was proof – if he needed it – that the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss will be under even greater scrutiny at United.

According to recent reports, responding, Pochettino remarked: 'We have young guys training with us. It’s not nice. It’s not good.

Sources indicate that 'What do they want to show? Yes, we were working on shape. We were very organised. What is the point of doing something that can be very dangerous?

'I don't want to be upset, but I think it's a process the club is caring a lot about.'.

Pochettino’s first training session with them at Carrington was ambushed by a drone shooting video footage that was posted online.

Having only trained for a couple of hours on Thursday, Pochettino worked with the players between 11.30am and 2pm on Friday.

‘The training session was a little bit longer than it normally is in (match day) minus two,’ said Pochettino at his opening pre-match press conference, admitting that he had not even had a chance to shower beforehand.

Pochettino worked with his new players between 11.30am and 2pm on Friday.

Pochettino took training for the third day running at Carrington on Saturday morning, before United travelled on the team bus to their hotel where they had dinner and a pre-match meeting last night.

On Sunday he faces a massive first game as United boss in front of the cameras at Anfield at the end of a dizzying fortnight.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Spain's Supreme Court has refused LaLiga's appeal, making final the annulment of the August 2021 assembly vote on the CVC deal, a case won by Real Madrid and Athletic Club.
  • Sources indicate that spain’s Supreme Court has thrown out LaLiga’s cassation appeal against the Madrid Provincial Court judgment on the CVC operation.
  • Industry observers note that the decision closes a five-year legal fight over that single vote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spain's Supreme Court has refused LaLiga's appeal, making final the annulment of the August 2021 assembly vote on the CVC deal, a case won by Real Madrid and Athletic Club. It is a legal win for the two clubs, but the later December 2021 approval behind LALIGA Impulso remains in force.

Sources indicate that spain’s Supreme Court has thrown out LaLiga’s cassation appeal against the Madrid Provincial Court judgment on the CVC operation. The General Assembly resolution of 12 August 2021, which approved the deal, therefore stays void for good. Real Madrid and Athletic Club brought the winning case. LaLiga now carries the costs of the failed appeal.

Industry observers note that the decision closes a five-year legal fight over that single vote. In August 2021, Barcelona, Athletic Club and Real Madrid jointly announced a challenge to the resolution. They argued it broke Royal Decree-Law 5/2015 and was passed through a highly irregular process.

Real Madrid described the annulled resolution as one of huge economic significance. In the club’s account, it was passed before clubs had enough information to judge the scope, impact and consequences of changes to the operation. The club also highlighted the court’s remark that LaLiga’s appeal tried to replace the Provincial Court’s view with LaLiga’s own self-interested view.

LaLiga reads the decision more narrowly. The annulled assembly approved the term sheet of the CVC project, and the appeal fell for lack of cassation interest. LaLiga remarked the court issued a procedural order rather than a judgment endorsing the Provincial Court’s reasoning, and did not examine the substance of the case.

It has been revealed that the deal itself does not depend on the annulled vote. LaLiga’s General Assembly approved the LALIGA Impulso project later, on 10 December 2021. Under the deal, clubs received around €2bn in exchange for a share of the value of the competition’s audiovisual rights over 50 years. A latest firm set up by LaLiga and the fund manages that arrangement. Real Madrid, Barcelona and Athletic Club rejected it and stayed out.

Sources indicate that those December resolutions have survived their own court test. In June 2026, Section 18 of the Madrid Provincial Court rejected in full the appeal by Athletic Club and Real Madrid against them. It upheld the first-instance judgment of 19 February 2024 and ordered both clubs to pay the costs of that hearing. The court found that clubs still own their audiovisual rights, while LaLiga sells them collectively under the law. It also ruled that creating LaLiga Group International, owned jointly by LaLiga and CVC, did not breach the Sports Law or LaLiga’s statutes.

It has been revealed that that leaves the practical picture largely unchanged. Iusport, a Spanish sports-law outlet, described the Supreme Court order as having no practical effect on the LaLiga–CVC deal. The ruling still matters for how LaLiga is run, because it confirms that one of its assembly votes on the operation was unlawful. The league insists it respects court decisions and will keep defending the agreements backed by most of its clubs.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Historically, goalkeeper has been a position of strength for the United States men's national team, to the extent that during the time of Tim Howard and Brad Guzan, both were playing Premier League soccer, but only one could start between the sticks. Things have changed since then, with numerous keepers coming through the ranks over the years, with most playing domestically or sitting on the bench for stronger European sides. However, that could be coming to an end for the team.

It has been revealed that during Mauricio Pochettino's tenure, Matt Freese has been his starting keeper, taking over during the Gold Cup and starting every game that he was available for until the September/October international window, when Pochettino used Diego Kochen and Brian Schwake. Kochen, who is playing his first season of first-team soccer at Lyngby in Denmark (where center back Neil Pierre also got his first taste of senior soccer), got the clean sheet against Mexico during that camp and turned that into a start against Haiti in Concacaf Nations League play in his native Miami, setting the USMNT up well to advance to the semifinals of the tournament.

Following that match, Kochen acknowledged that the USMNT squad has done a lot to put him in this position, and he'll know that even if Pochettino won't be the manager choosing the lineups, performances like this one will be important for how the USMNT keeper picture looks moving forward.

According to recent reports, "I feel like I've grown quite a lot," Kochen mentioned following the match, reflecting on his adjustment to the national team. "I'm getting used to competing at the international level, but I've just got to give it to my team because they've been unbelievable. They make it so easy to just come out here and play free and be me, so without them, this wouldn't be possible.".

In a recent development, his growth is evident; one of the first things that comes to mind when watching the 20-year-old is his poise. Kochen had the ball at his feet plenty, completing all 20 of his passes to help send the attack on its way, and also made the two saves that he needed to on a mostly quiet night. His age also demonstrated when Haiti scored with him out of position, a goal that was called back for offside, but you take the good with the bad for young players because that's a learning moment, and as he earns more reps at the senior level, those are the kind of mistakes that can be ironed out.

Recent findings suggest that "I'm not saying he hasn't played games in Barcelona, but at the senior level, every game he plays, he gets better and better and better," one of Kochen's coaches, Andreas Bjelland, told CBS Sports. "Because understanding the full-pitch play, and not only being on the line, just taking shots, and being a training goalie, but now he's playing for points every week. He's growing as a player, as a person, and as somebody we can trust more and more in the stuff we do. So it's nice to see that it has come to this ... It's quite impressive.".

It has been revealed that you can't teach poise, and spending more than five years in the Barcelona system highlights in how Kochen carries himself. It's becoming more common in American soccer for young players to test themselves abroad or to get into Major League Soccer teams at a younger age, and when they succeed, it goes a long way developmentally, as Kochen's case shows.

Recent findings suggest that "He is a person who trusts himself a lot. That's also why he's a good goalie, that at such a young age he hasn't that significant of a doubt of himself," Mikkel Jespersen, Lyngby's other coach said. "He knows what he's capable of doing, and that's really crucial as a goalie: that you trust yourself and know what things you are doing is something that can succeed in a longer period.".

Industry observers note that while it's unknown what the next USMNT manager will value in a keeper, being able to perform in an uncertain environment with your coach having one foot out the door is something that will go a long way for Kochen's chances. In keeper terms, Kochen has plenty of time ahead of him, as players at his position regularly play until their late 30s or early 40s, so if he can continue this trajectory, the question of who protects the net could be solved for the foreseeable future.

Recent findings suggest that of course, that's a lot of projecting, but when the next generation of the USMNT is developing at an astounding rate, it's only natural to think about where players like Kochen could end up. Doing this in only his first season of professional soccer is already impressive, but the best is yet to come.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Representatives of Serbia's student-led movement were sworn in as lawmakers on Tuesday, just over four weeks after they ended Serbia's strongman leader Aleksandar Vucic's 14 years of rule.

The Students' List candidates officially took their seats in the inaugural parliamentary session as the first step for the youth-backed party toward forming Serbia's new government.

Recent findings suggest that the movement holds 140 seats in the 250-member parliament while Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) holds 103. The remaining seats belong to ethnic minority parties.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Hundreds gathered outside the parliament building in the capital Belgrade, to show their support for the student-backed lawmakers, most of whom are teachers, professors and other professionals with little or no political experience.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, SNS candidates were met with a negative reaction from the crowd. A woman in the crowd poured yogurt over an SNS member's head as she climbed the steps to the parliament entrance.

According to Serbian media, the newly elected lawmakers have been preparing for their first session for days. They will face veteran opposition politicians, including Aleksandar Vucic, who became the opposition leader after his defeat.

The Students' List will have 90 days to name a prime minister, present their programme and form a government, once the parliament is formed.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that the movement unites left- and right-wingers, pro-European and pro-Russian forces. It is focused on making changes in domestic politics and wants to advance European Union accession talks by implementing real reforms. The List opposes sanctions on Russia and the recognition of Kosovo — positions that almost the entire population of Serbia agrees with.

They pledged to improve healthcare, boost education and double the defense budget, along with many other reforms.

Recent findings suggest that the election of a new parliamentary speaker will also lead to the appointment of a new acting president. The speaker has held the role since Vucic resigned in September to run for prime minister.

A snap presidential election must be called by November 27 and held by December 27.

Both parties are expected to put forward presidential candidates, but Vucic cannot seek another term because the constitution limits presidents to two terms in office.

Mathematics Álvaro Lozano-Robledo thought the Riemann hypothesis was out of AI’s reach for now.Credit: Bri Diaz/UConn Photo.

It has been revealed that the news came on a Friday — and it was ground-shaking. For months, reports have mounted of artificial-intelligence models toppling some of the toughest problems in mathematics, plunging the field into turmoil. But the latest claim was the most shocking yet: an AI model had helped to solve the field’s most famous open problem, the Riemann hypothesis.

AI is ‘the end of mathematics as we know it’ — where does the field go next?

AI is ‘the end of mathematics as we know it’ — where does the field go next?

The proof was released on 20 November by mathematician Levent Alpöge at AI giant Anthropic in San Francisco, California, who used an advanced version of the firm’s Claude model. It came in the form of 17 million lines of code in the open-source programming language Lean, which translates mathematical arguments into computer-certifiable code. In a matter of hours, a separate set of mathematicians rushed out a human-written proof of the Riemann hypothesis, which is in the branch of number theory and pertains to the randomness of prime numbers.

Alpöge’s proof has been independently verified by the non-profit organization behind Lean and the Mathlib Initiative, which runs the reference library of formalized mathematics results written in Lean. “We have full confidence that Alpöge’s proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct, and we congratulate him,” the community remarked in a statement on 21 November.

It has been revealed that the mathematics community has broadly accepted the claim, although responses differ wildly. Some celebrate Alpöge’s achievement, but others see the development as proof that humans are fighting against machines for the future of mathematics.

Nature hears reactions from four mathematicians on what solving the Riemann hypothesis means to them.

Mathematician Tasmin Chu is part of the Association for Human Mathematics, whose members commit to doing AI-free research.Credit: Elizabeth Xiao.

Tasmin Chu, PhD student in mathematics at the California Institute of Technology in Pasadena.

Sources indicate that A technology that can autonomously prove the Riemann hypothesis is no trivial matter. I think that it is imperative our society acts to pause AI development as soon as possible. Over the past year, mathematical institutions have faced the impossible task of adapting to the rapidly changing capabilities of AI in real time.

According to recent reports, it’s enormously disruptive for early-career researchers — the people who are the intellectual future of our field. Soon other sectors of society will face the same issues.

My reaction is grave concern. AI companies urgently require democratic oversight. I do not think AI’s encroachment into math is inevitable, nor is the death of human mathematical practice inevitable. It’s a choice to disempower ourselves, just as it’s a choice to continue building these technologies despite grave safety concerns. I continue to practice mathematics without LLMs, because I believe it’s critical that scientific inquiry continues in the hands of human beings. Many of us at the Association for Human Mathematics — whose organizing committee I am on — are collectively making the same decision.

Harini Desiraju, postdoc in mathematics at the University of Warwick, UK.

Given the events of the past few months, this news wasn't entirely a surprise, but we need to wait to understand the Lean proof and let the experts verify it. It is several million lines of code, after all.

I am not a number theorist, so I might not have the same emotional attachment to the Riemann hypothesis. Nevertheless, I have deep appreciation for the ubiquity and the importance of the problem in several areas of maths and physics.

In a recent development, as for the recent events, I want to distinguish between formal proofs versus knowledge. It is an impressive feat to solve such a problem. However, because it is a Lean proof over millions of lines, it is going to take a while before the community gets real understanding, and validity of the proof. With an AI-independent approach available as well, it could present a great opportunity for discovery of newly introduced ideas and mathematics. We need to see how it all plays out.

It has been revealed that there is another discussion to be had, which involves the role of frontier labs in research. Most of us see the potential benefits of this technology, but it is of utmost importance that we work towards a future where the agency is with the scientific community and not a couple of companies.

Mathematician Marcus Du Sautoy is anxious about what’s next for his field.Credit: David Levenson/Getty.

Marcus Du Sautoy, mathematician and professor for the public understanding of science at the University of Oxford, UK.

According to recent reports, it was real mix of emotions. A part of me indicates, how exciting to be alive when this great problem was solved! I think even when Fermat’s last theorem was solved, we had the same excitement and the same melancholy: that great motivator is gone.

Mixed in with that, is the complete surprise that it ended up being proved this way. If you’d asked me three months ago, I would never have predicted it.

There’s quite a lot of anxiety about what ‘math 2.0’ is going to look like.

Xin Zhang, assistant professor in mathematics at the University of Hong Kong.

At the Estadio Nuevo Vivero on Wednesday 18 November, Álvaro Cervera’s side booked a place in the second round of the Copa del Rey. The tie had been postponed twice, first after the train accident in Toledo province and then after the death of Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel on 3 November, who was remembered with a minute’s silence.

Industry observers note that cervera started a line-up made up largely of reserves. It still produced a scoreline Tenerife had never recorded in 260 Copa del Rey matches, according to elDiario.es (Canarias Ahora). About 3,000 spectators watched, around 20 per cent of the stadium’s capacity.

Grant-Leon Ranos opened the scoring in the sixth minute from a Marc Mateu assist. Juanjo Sánchez added a second a minute later. Ranos struck again in the 38th minute, set up by Gerard Valentín.

Carlos Beitia pulled one back for Badajoz in the 49th minute. Roko Jureškin was then sent off in the 58th minute. Ten-man Tenerife still extended the lead through substitute Iván Chapela in the 69th minute, assisted by Martin Pečar.

According to recent reports, jorge Barba replied for the hosts in the 74th minute from a Manuel Hernández assist. Víctor Moreno completed the scoring deep into stoppage time, with Álvarez providing the pass.

The Segunda Federación side went into the tie third in their group. They were also unbeaten in seven league matches in a row.

It has been revealed that tenerife have now come through their opening Copa del Rey tie in eight seasons in a row. The win followed a 2-0 victory over AD Ceuta FC. Before that came a run of draws against FC Andorra, Sabadell, Celta de Vigo II and Girona.

This was the first meeting between the clubs in the cup. They had played each other 22 times in Segunda División. Tenerife won ten of those games, Badajoz eight, and four ended level. Tenerife’s previous visit to Badajoz, on 30 March 2003, ended in a 2-1 defeat under David Amaral.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gian Piero Gasperini is ‘happy and proud’ that his Roma gamble paid off with a 2-2 Champions League draw away to PSG. ‘If we stayed in the game, the second half would be decisive.’.

The Giallorossi were the underdogs going into Parc des Princes, against the side that has dominated the Champions League in the last two years and had won all four of their games so far this season.

There were some huge surprises in the starting XI, as Malen, Paulo Dybala and Bryan Cristante were all on the bench, while Niccolò Pisilli was picked behind Santiago Castro to follow Vitinha around.

“I am very happy and proud of this evening’s performance. It was obvious we would not change our approach even against the best team, and PSG are certainly the best team in Europe right now,” confessed Gasperini on Sky Sport Italia.

In a recent development, “They not only have a lot of talent at their disposal, but also great organisation and a variety of different systems they can call upon. It was a very important match for us, but I will watch it back, because there was a lot to learn from it that can help us going forward in Serie A and the Champions League.”.

Nonetheless, Mario Hermoso gave them the early lead after five minutes, turned around by Illia Zabarnyi’s free header on a corner and the Ousmane Dembele penalty, until substitute Donyell Malen converted another spot-kick for the Vitinha handling offence.

Was it because Roma have shown a tendency to fall away in the final 20 minutes of European games with this very tiring style of football, so he wanted their quality off the bench?

“Malen has played many games, including international duty, so it was only fair to give Castro a chance. It’s also true that the blueprint was to introduce him in the second half, which is when the games are decided,” explained Gasperini.

Industry observers note that “Dybala had also made his comeback against Parma after more than a month out, so he needed to be looked after. Cristante played a lot too, but I introduced Pisilli, who was fantastic. It’s not as if these players were replaced by someone inferior.

“We knew that if we stayed in the game, then the second half would become decisive. PSG introduced Dembele and other players of the highest quality, so for a while the game was going our way, and at the end we couldn’t wait for the final whistle to come.”.

When Fabio Capello read the starting XI, he wondered if Gasperini and Roma were surrendering the Champions League to focus on Serie A, but there was a plan behind it.

“I am particularly satisfied tonight,” laughed Gasperini.

“I knew there were some risks, but not for me, because I see these lads improving, and if we can get through games like this, it’s a massive boost for everyone.”.

Soulé was a player who seemed to be on the way out of Roma last season, but has instead managed to go from strength to strength.

“Along with being a strong player, he is also a very positive guy who learns promptly and wants to improve. He is only 23 years old, is much more complete now that he used to be, as he played on the left, behind the two strikers, whereas before he wouldn’t leave his little area.

Recent findings suggest that “He is achieving maturity now, and I am so happy for him, because it’s been a couple of months that he has really progressed. My job is to get the best out of these players, but I cannot add characteristics that they do not have, I just need to help them to flourish,” assured Gasperini.

Finally, he was asked if Roma are focused more on Serie A or the Champions League?

“We let nothing slip,” he concluded.

Real Madrid have extended the contracts of Aurélien Tchouaméni and Arda Güler until June 2032, a day apart. With captain Fede Valverde also reportedly agreeing new terms, the club are securing their core midfield for years to come.

Real Madrid have committed two midfield regulars to long-term deals in the space of 24 hours. Güler’s announcement came first, and Aurélien Tchouaméni’s followed.

According to recent reports, both players are part of the core of Mourinho’s midfield. The renewals keep them at the club for six more seasons.

Tchouaméni arrived in 2022 and has made 205 appearances for the club. He has won eight trophies in that time. They include one Champions League, two Club World Cups and two UEFA Super Cups. He has also lifted one LaLiga, one Copa del Rey and one Spanish Super Cup.

Sources indicate that his standing goes beyond the club. He has 50 France caps and won the 2021 Nations League. The latest contract is worth around €9 million net per season, GOAL reported. The agreement came after interest from Manchester United.

It has been revealed that güler’s record covers a shorter spell. He was 18 when he joined. He has 38 caps for Turkey. In September he was named Breakthrough Player of the 2025-26 Champions League. His latest salary is reportedly about €8m a year.

In a recent development, the two profiles differ. Tchouaméni is an established international with a full set of club honours. Güler is a younger player whose contract now runs almost nine years from his arrival. Tying both to the same end date suggests a midfield the club intend to keep together.

The club may not be finished. Captain Fede Valverde has agreed to extend his contract from 2029 to 2031, according to GOAL. The newly introduced deal will make him one of the squad’s highest earners. An announcement is expected soon, as Madrid work on further renewals after Güler and Tchouaméni.

If Valverde’s extension is confirmed, none of the three midfielders would have a contract ending before 2031. That would remove contract questions over a key part of the squad for several seasons. The two completed renewals arrived during the build-up to a busy run of home matches.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia on Tuesday noted it had created a board-level national security and export-control committee.

This follows the scandal surrounding former CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned last week over extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China and working to help ensure higher quality chips crucial to AI development made it to the Chinese market.

The events have heightened oversight of the US tech giant and its importance to national security, as well as wiping several hundred billion dollars off the stock market valuation of what investors treat as the world's most valuable organization in the space of a month.

Since Huang's resignation, some investors — including Elon Musk and Donald Trump — have voiced concern that his departure could leave Nvidia and America's AI sector in peril and are now calling for his return. Huang on Tuesday, expressed regret for "serious mistakes" in his personal life before declaring he would be "honored" to return if the firm's board of directors thought that was "in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America.".

Nvidia is calling the fresh group its National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee.

Suzanne Nora Johnson, a former vice chair at Goldman Sachs, will chair the committee, joined by fellow directors Stephen Neal, a former CEO of a law firm, John Dabiri, a professor of aeronautics and mechanical engineering at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech).

In a recent development, the committee will meet at least once every quarter. It will also incorporate independent legal, national security and trade compliance experts.

Nvidia already has a lower-level National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team; these groups will report to the board-level committee.

"We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation," Board Chair Harvey Jones mentioned in a statement.

The tech giant did not explicitly link the decision to November's developments and Huang's rapid fall from grace, but the timing seemed conspicuous.

The decision was declared hours ahead of Nvidia publishing its third-quarter results, with its still-stratospheric share price having fallen roughly 28% in the past month.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US President Donald Trump, whom Huang was influential in persuading to allow the export of better-quality Nvidia chips to China than other US companies and officials deemed prudent, welcomed Nvidia's move on arrival in the Philippines on Tuesday.

"Yes, that's a good idea. It's a great organization," he stated during a photo opportunity at a Manila meeting with the other "Quad" leaders from Australia, India and Japan. "It's a great idea.".

Recent findings suggest that trump reportedly owned Nvidia stock worth tens of millions of dollars before the share price fell. He also owns shares in other big tech companies.

In a recent development, huang resigned last week after admitting to extramarital affairs in a message to Nvidia employees. This followed widespread reports, seemingly based on US and other intelligence, that one of the affairs was with a woman who used to lead a Singapore-based cloud computing tech giant.

Sources indicate that that company, Megaspseed International, is a major Nvidia client and is suspected of diverting advanced chips to China in violation of US export controls. Intelligence officials also suspect Huang's partner of being an asset of Chinese intelligence services.

The reporting on the case also seems to show these suspicions had been known to US officials and other countries, including Singapore, for roughly a year.

Man Utd show fight on night of chaos to give Carrick a glimpse of hope
